target.title: fix: config rejects compaction.enabled, leaving auto-compaction impossible to disable
target.body:
Closes #110065

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users setting `"enabled": false` under `agents.defaults.compaction` in `openclaw.json` would have their entire config rejected (`agents.defaults.compaction: Invalid input`) when running any gateway command. The session runtime already reads `compaction.enabled` (defaulting to `true`), but the strict config schema did not accept the key — so there was no way to disable auto-compaction through configuration at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

Of the three options the issue proposed (accept the field, delete the reader, or document the limitation), accepting the field is the only one that makes the existing runtime capability reachable. The boolean is added to the zod schema, `AgentCompactionConfig` type, schema labels/help, and is plumbed into `applyAgentCompactionSettingsFromConfig` as a non-persisted runtime override next to the existing `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` overrides.

Deliberate boundary: only an explicit `false` is propagated. `true` is already the runtime default, and pushing `true` as a runtime override would outrank `applyAgentAutoCompactionGuard`'s later `setCompactionEnabled(false)` in the settings merge — re-enabling auto-compaction in exactly the silent-overflow cases the guard exists to protect (#75799). A regression test pins this ordering.

## User Impact

Operators can now put `agents.defaults.compaction.enabled: false` in `openclaw.json` to disable auto-compaction (e.g. when an external context engine or provider-side compaction owns it). Configs that set the field no longer fail validation. No behavior change for anyone not setting the field.

## Evidence

Targeted test lanes (all green):

```
pnpm vitest run src/config/zod-schema.agent-defaults.test.ts src/agents/agent-settings.test.ts \
  src/config/config.compaction-settings.test.ts src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  140 passed (140)
```

New tests: schema accepts `enabled: false`/`true` and rejects non-boolean values; `enabled: false` reaches `SettingsManager.getCompactionEnabled()`; explicit `true` does **not** override the auto-compaction guard.

Additionally, a 9-case before/after acceptance matrix was driven through the real `validateConfigObject()` on both `origin/main` and this branch, scored by an external QC harness (Synthia anchor-check panel — objective pass/fail checks only, no LLM judging):

```
  [PASS] bug-reproduced-on-main       main rejects enabled:false with ['agents.defaults.compaction: Unrecognized key: "enabled"']
  [PASS] after/issue-repro-enabled-false     issue #110065 repro: compaction.enabled: false must be accepted
  [PASS] after/enabled-true                  explicit compaction.enabled: true accepted
  [PASS] after/enabled-false-with-siblings   enabled: false composes with existing tuning fields
  [PASS] after/reject-enabled-string         compaction.enabled: "off" (string) must be rejected
  [PASS] after/reject-enabled-number         compaction.enabled: 0 (number) must be rejected
  [PASS] after/reject-enabled-null           compaction.enabled: null must be rejected
  [PASS] after/regression-existing-fields    pre-existing compaction config still accepted unchanged
  [PASS] after/regression-strictness-preserved  unknown compaction keys still rejected (schema stays strict)
  [PASS] after/regression-empty-config       empty config still accepted
  [PASS] no-regression-drift                 pre-existing cases changed acceptance: none

Synthia QC panel: 11/11 checks passed, anchor fidelity 100.0
```

`pnpm check`: typecheck prod/scripts/test-root all pass. The one lint failure (`extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts` consistent-return) and one vitest failure (`src/config/sessions/entry-freshness.test.ts`) are pre-existing on `origin/main` (verified in a clean worktree at b7dd330bd3) and untouched by this diff.

**Real CLI behavior proof** (source checkout via `pnpm openclaw`, isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, scratch paths redacted). The config file contains only `{ "agents": { "defaults": { "compaction": { "enabled": false } } } }`:

```console
# BEFORE — origin/main @ 0546e15c2e
$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.compaction
File: <config-path>/openclaw.json
Problem:
  - agents.defaults.compaction: Unrecognized key: "enabled"
Fix: openclaw doctor --fix

# AFTER — this branch, identical config
$ openclaw config validate
Config valid: <config-path>/openclaw.json

$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.compaction
{
  "enabled": false
}

$ openclaw status
OpenClaw status
(renders the full status table normally; on main this command exits with the validation error above)
```

The `config get` read goes through the same validated runtime config snapshot the gateway and embedded runner consume, and the propagation into the session settings manager (`getCompactionEnabled() === false`, guard ordering intact) is pinned by the new `src/agents/agent-settings.test.ts` cases against the real `SettingsManager`.

**Review follow-ups addressed** (from the earlier ClawSweeper pass):
- Config doc baseline regenerated (`pnpm config:docs:gen`; `pnpm config:docs:check` now passes — it was drifting on this branch).
- Guard precedence documented: schema help and `docs/gateway/config-agents.md` now state explicitly that `enabled: true` does not override the auto-compaction safety guard (overflow-prone providers / context-engine-owned compaction still force-disable).

On the remaining runtime-observation ask, stated plainly: there is currently **no supported runtime diagnostic that surfaces the effective auto-compaction flag** — `AgentSessionCompaction.autoCompactionEnabled` has zero consumers, and no CLI/status/log line prints it. The closest supported observations are the real-CLI `config get` above (the same snapshot the runner consumes) and the settings-manager propagation tests. A live-session observation would require a model-driven run; if maintainers want it, I'm happy to add a small diagnostic surface (e.g. include the flag in session status output) as a follow-up — that felt like scope creep to bundle here.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where feature-branch Testbox checks could fail with Plugin SDK baseline drift even when the same drift already reproduced on clean current main. Independent PRs each replaced one whole-surface checksum, so later merge order could leave the combined source and committed checksum out of sync.

The tracked contract manifest now stores one deterministic hash per public Plugin SDK entrypoint. Independent entrypoint changes modify independent lines and merge in either order, while concurrent changes to the same entrypoint remain a real merge conflict that requires regeneration against the combined source. Full JSON and JSONL snapshots remain gitignored local inspection artifacts.

## User Impact

No user-visible product change. Maintainers keep unintended public API drift protection without downstream branches paying for aggregate-checksum merge races.

- Clean-main reproduction before this fix: Plugin SDK API baseline drift failed in Testbox run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29618356643.
- Regenerated clean-main checksum difference: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29618421112.

## Summary

Fixes #109985

Two fixes:
1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — call `response.body?.cancel()` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message instead of a raw SyntaxError.

## Real behavior proof

### 1. qa-lab response body cancel

**Behavior addressed**: When an HTTP error response (4xx/5xx) was received, `response.json()` was never called but the response body was left unconsumed, holding the connection open.

**Real environment tested**: Node.js test runner (vitest) with mocked `fetch`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:

target.body:
Closes #110065

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users setting `"enabled": false` under `agents.defaults.compaction` in `openclaw.json` would have their entire config rejected (`agents.defaults.compaction: Invalid input`) when running any gateway command. The session runtime already reads `compaction.enabled` (defaulting to `true`), but the strict config schema did not accept the key — so there was no way to disable auto-compaction through configuration at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

Of the three options the issue proposed (accept the field, delete the reader, or document the limitation), accepting the field is the only one that makes the existing runtime capability reachable. The boolean is added to the zod schema, `AgentCompactionConfig` type, schema labels/help, and is plumbed into `applyAgentCompactionSettingsFromConfig` as a non-persisted runtime override next to the existing `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` overrides.

Deliberate boundary: only an explicit `false` is propagated. `true` is already the runtime default, and pushing `true` as a runtime override would outrank `applyAgentAutoCompactionGuard`'s later `setCompactionEnabled(false)` in the settings merge — re-enabling auto-compaction in exactly the silent-overflow cases the guard exists to protect (#75799). A regression test pins this ordering.

## User Impact

Operators can now put `agents.defaults.compaction.enabled: false` in `openclaw.json` to disable auto-compaction (e.g. when an external context engine or provider-side compaction owns it). Configs that set the field no longer fail validation. No behavior change for anyone not setting the field.

target.title: fix(google-video): cancel unread response body on download error
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Added `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw in `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` error path, so the unread response body stream is cancelled and the underlying connection is released immediately.

**What NOT changed**: No change to any other provider (OpenAI, Bedrock, etc.). No change to success paths. No change to retry or timeout logic. No new dependencies.

Fixes #109978

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` receives a non-OK HTTP response (e.g. 403, 429, 500), the `response.body` readable stream remains unconsumed. Node.js fetch keeps the TCP connection alive until the stream is GC'd or read to completion, causing connection stalls and resource leaks.

**Root Cause**: Missing `response.body.cancel()` in the error path of `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` in `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.ts`.

**Solution**: Call `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing the error. The optional chaining handles null-body responses gracefully. The `.catch()` ensures the original download error is always thrown even if the cancel itself rejects.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0, OpenClaw 2026.7.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run the unit test suite to confirm existing behavior
cd /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts

# Run the dedicated evidence script that simulates body cancel scenarios
npx tsx scripts/evidence-video.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
=== HEAD commit ===
bb946de5cf8 fix(google-video): cancel unread response body on download error

--- Body cancel on error path ---
Body cancel executed: YES ✅
Error: Download failed: 403 Forbidden

--- Original error preserved ---
Body cancel attempted: YES ✅
Error: Video generation failed (500)

--- Null body (optional chaining) ---
Null body handled: YES (via ?.) ✅
Error: Bad request

--- All HTTP error status codes ---
Status 400: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 401: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 403: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 429: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 500: body cancelled=OK ✅
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All body cancel scenarios pass. The body is cancelled before throw for all HTTP error status codes. The original download error is preserved even when `body.cancel()` rejects. Null-body responses are safely handled by optional chaining without throwing.

**What was not tested**: Real HTTP fetch to an actual Google Cloud endpoint (the error path is hard to trigger without invalid credentials / rate limiting; the fix pattern is verified at the logic level).

target.title: perf(ci): cut the pre-fan-out critical path and bin canonical main runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With the vitest whales gone (top job 187s), the measured wall of a canonical main run (11.5 min, run 29592647843) is dominated by everything *around* the tests:

1. `runner-admission` — a GitHub-hosted 90s sleep — queued ~1.7 min on the hosted pool before its sleep even began, and every job in the run waited behind it.
2. The 82-job named matrix drained the Blacksmith pool for ~4.5 min (job starts trickled from minute 5.2 to 9.7).
3. The TUI PTY harness file booted its three suite PTYs serially.

## Why This Change Was Made

Maintainer-requested ("do 1,2,3"): cut the pre-fan-out critical path, consolidate the main-run matrix, batch PTY sessions.

## User Impact

- Every canonical run loses the hosted-queue + serial-sleep head (~2–2.5 min expected): the debounce now runs as a residual sleep at the tail of `preflight` (usually 0s, since preflight's real work exceeds the 90s window), preserving the cancel-before-fan-out semantics with only one 4 vCPU runner at risk. `security-fast` starts immediately.
- Canonical main pushes use the compact bin plan (~20 bins instead of 82 named jobs) — identical coverage, far less pool drain. `workflow_dispatch`/release-gate runs keep the full named matrix for release tooling.
- The PTY harness file halves (10.2s → ~4.9s locally) by booting its three fixtures concurrently.

## Evidence

- Head decomposition from run 29592647843: admission started +1.7 min (hosted queue), preflight +3.4 min, first check +5.2 min, last check start +9.7 min. The new topology removes the hosted hop entirely and overlaps the debounce with preflight's work.
- Workflow parsed and machine-verified post-edit: 24 jobs, `preflight` need-free with the epoch/gate steps first/last, `security-fast` ungated, `openclaw/ci-gate` requires preflight+security.
- Guard test rewritten to enshrine the new invariant (debounce gate step at preflight tail, no standalone admission job on the critical path); planner/guards/changed-plan suites green — 274 passed, 1 skipped.
- PTY: 21/21 tests, 3× repeat runs green at 4.8–6.1s (baseline 10.2s); `allSettled` boot keeps partial-failure cleanup leak-free; slow-startup ordering assertion is strictly stronger than the old sequential waits. (Original scope note: the harness file was already session-batched since #85485; the genuinely expensive `tui-pty-local` file is stateful-by-design — every test asserts `/exit` semantics or restarts the Gateway — and is documented as needing a design pass, not a mechanical merge.)
- `docs/ci.md` updated (job table, fail-fast order, gate contract). Codex autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): first pass caught a stale docs claim, fixed; final pass clean.

target.title: fix(feishu): bound sender name cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Fixes an issue where high-volume Feishu bots could retain an unbounded number of sender-name cache entries inside the ten-minute TTL window.**
- **Affected surface / workflow:** sender attribution for inbound Feishu bot events.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** `senderNameCache` had per-entry expiry but no maximum size, so a burst of unique sender IDs could grow the map without a hard bound.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** large groups and high-traffic bots can encounter many unique senders before entries expire, increasing process memory with no upper limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix
- **Complete shipped solution:** cap the sender-name cache at 500 entries and prune the oldest entry after successful insertions.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the cache owner now enforces a hard retention bound in addition to the existing TTL.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** the 500-entry limit matches Feishu's existing group-name cache policy and uses the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** sender ID type selection, permission handling, name precedence, and the ten-minute TTL are unchanged.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** no public API or configuration changes; an evicted sender simply performs the existing contact lookup again.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** run high-cardinality Feishu bot workloads with a bounded sender-name cache.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** recently inserted sender names remain cached and reuse the existing TTL.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** no external Feishu tenant credentials were used; the live proof exercised the production resolver and client-construction path against a local HTTP-backed client boundary.

target.title: fix(telegram): prevent gateway CPU spin on immediate empty polls
target.body:
No linked issue — this is a small, production-reproduced reliability fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Telegram polling through a local or custom Bot API endpoint could see the gateway consume an entire CPU core when that endpoint returned successful empty `getUpdates` responses immediately instead of holding the requested long poll.

## Why This Change Was Made

Successful empty polls now have a one-second start-to-start minimum, using the worker's existing abort-aware sleep. Non-empty batches still drain immediately, and retry, spool, acknowledgement, offset, configuration, and protocol behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

Telegram polling can no longer hammer the Bot API and starve the gateway when an endpoint repeatedly returns empty successes too quickly. Normal long polls and polls containing updates gain no added delay, and shutdown remains immediate.

## Evidence

Production incident (sanitized, 2026-05-22):

- Before: the gateway held about one CPU core, health reported `eventLoop.degraded=true` for CPU, and `strace` showed thousands of local Bot API syscalls over a few seconds.
- After applying the equivalent one-second empty-success floor and restarting: health reported `eventLoop.degraded=false`; observed CPU core ratios settled at 0.062 and then 0.032, and gateway threads were sleeping.
- Current operational check with that equivalent local hotfix: `ok=true`, `eventLoop.degraded=false`, CPU core ratio 0.077, and both Telegram polling accounts connected. The PR-head source was not installed on production for this validation.

Exact PR-head controlled runtime proof (sanitized, 2026-07-17):

- Verified clean SHA `834efa45f731df102496069136902bc88ebfe16d`; the runtime entry's `HEAD` blob and worktree blob both resolved to `93ba5914b1b95632dead69a28a0e8e27614037c3`, with empty `git status` before and after.

- Pointed the Worker's real HTTP transport at a loopback-only Bot API stand-in that immediately returned `HTTP 200 {"ok":true,"result":[]}`. The request carried `timeout: 30` and `limit: 100`; the credential was synthetic and no external network or production service was used.
- Sent stop immediately after the fifth empty success, while the Worker was in the new empty-success cadence sleep, exercising its abort-aware path.

target.title: fix(cli): exit cleanly on startup migration refusal
target.body:
## Summary

- report the three planned startup migration/config/plugin refusal reasons at their owner, then throw `ExitError(1)` so `ensureConfigReady` uses its existing typed `runtime.exit` path
- add a hermetic child-process regression that exercises a real conflicting plugin-state migration, requires exit status 1 with no signal, verifies the refusal appears exactly once, and confirms the startup migration lease is released
- audit the core `DatabaseSync` migration/checkpoint paths for throw-time handle leaks; every direct handle is already closed by `finally`, so no unrelated migration refactor is included

This PR was originally stacked on #110200. That prerequisite has now merged as `748fc044192a1c98d8344ea6682a3f38dd7ef384`; the branch was rebased onto `origin/main` at `82fa956d5a22c65d0dd9f2bfc5ff964e45c9728e`, and the already-applied `ce6e200aaa2` commit dropped from this PR's history. The landing dependency is satisfied.

Refs #109831.

## What Problem This Solves

Startup migration, invalid-config, and plugin-verification refusals were ordinary `Error`s. They bypassed the typed exit handling in `src/cli/program/config-guard.ts`, reached the generic `src/entry.ts` failure handler, and ended in its direct `process.exit(1)` path. In the reported supervised deployment, that path terminated with signal 11 / status 139 instead of a clean refusal status, turning a fail-closed migration result into a supervisor crash loop.

## Root Cause

The proven pre-fix control flow is:

1. `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` formatted an intentional readiness refusal but threw a plain `Error`.
2. `ensureConfigReady` only converts `ExitError` into `runtime.exit(error.code)`, so it rethrew the plain refusal.
3. `src/entry.ts` added `Could not start the CLI.` / `Reason:` formatting and called `process.exit(1)`.

The preflight's existing `finally` already releases its heartbeat and startup migration lease before the error leaves the owner. The fix preserves that unwind and hands the intentional refusal to the typed caller contract instead of treating it as an unexpected CLI startup failure.

The reporter's exact native signal source is not established without their core dump. This change fixes the incorrect refusal path and locks down the observable process contract; it does not claim to identify or patch the native module.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal owner must print the reason because the typed `ExitError` branch intentionally does not format errors, while the generic entry catch is no longer reached. Printing once immediately before throwing `ExitError(1)` preserves the complete operator guidance without duplicating the generic wrapper.

This is the narrow owner-boundary fix: unexpected preflight errors still use the generic failure handler, and gateway readiness remains fail-closed.

The core migration audit covered the direct `DatabaseSync` constructors in `src/infra/state-migrations.debug-proxy.ts`, `src/infra/state-migrations.task-sidecar-rows.ts`, and `src/infra/state-migrations.storage.ts`, plus the checkpoint database wrapper used by `src/infra/startup-migration-checkpoint.ts`. Each closes in `finally`, including throw paths. No plugin-owned code was changed.

## User Impact

When a startup migration gate refuses readiness, operators retain the full actionable refusal text exactly once. The CLI exits through the typed status-1 path, the migration lease is released, and supervisors see a normal non-zero exit rather than a signal in the covered regression environment.

## Evidence

### Rebase result

After #110200 merged, `git fetch origin main` and `git rebase origin/main` skipped its already-applied `ce6e200aaa2` commit and replayed only this PR's fix. Main advanced once during the proof window, so the branch was rebased a second time before the final proof.

`git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` on the published branch contains one commit:

```text
d0281e2cc2a fix(cli): exit cleanly on migration refusal
```

Final identities:

```text
origin/main=82fa956d5a22c65d0dd9f2bfc5ff964e45c9728e
head=d0281e2cc2a852f2c20903275fa7fa74ac996c92
```

### Real behavior proof — exact rebased head

Environment: Linux source checkout, Node `v25.9.0`, actual `src/entry.ts`, no provider/channel credentials, and an isolated realpathed temporary `HOME`, config, and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. The canonical plugin-state row had timestamp 2000 and value `{"version":1}`; the legacy sidecar held the same key with newer timestamp 3000 and divergent value `{"version":2}`. That is intentionally unresolved under the merged #109832 migration contract.

A Node supervisor wrapper used `spawnSync` with a 60-second timeout and captured the wait status and signal separately. It launched the actual gateway entry twice against the same unresolved state:

```text
node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway run --allow-unconfigured
```

Observed on exact head `d0281e2cc2a852f2c20903275fa7fa74ac996c92`:

```text
gateway_run_1 status=1 signal=none refusal_count=1 stale_lease_count=0 generic_wrapper_count=0
after_gateway_run_1 active_startup_migration_lease=false
gateway_run_2 status=1 signal=none refusal_count=1 stale_lease_count=0 generic_wrapper_count=0
after_gateway_run_2 active_startup_migration_lease=false
```

Redacted stderr from the first run:

```text
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Left plugin-state sidecar in place because 1 row differs from shared state without a newer canonical timestamp. First key: proof-plugin/proof-namespace/proof-key
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Left plugin-state sidecar in place because 1 row differs from shared state without a newer canonical timestamp. First key: proof-plugin/proof-namespace/proof-key
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

This proves both supervisor-observed gateway attempts exited with code 1 rather than a signal/status 139, printed the refusal headline exactly once on stderr, omitted the generic outer-entry wrapper, and released the startup migration lease. The second run acquired a fresh lease and did not report a stale/active lease.

### Doctor-path parity

The same exact-head wrapper and unresolved fixture then ran:

```text
node --import tsx src/entry.ts doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
```

Observed:

```text
doctor_fix status=0 signal=none stale_lease_count=0 active_startup_migration_lease=false
```

Doctor continues to report the unresolved migration without gating gateway readiness, exits normally, and releases its lease. Gateway remains fail-closed on the next startup attempt.

### Guard-boundary verification

The existing `ensureConfigReady` catch in `src/cli/program/config-guard.ts` intercepts `ExitError` and calls `runtime.exit(error.code)`. The live process transcript proves the refusal reaches that branch: the generic `[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.` wrapper count is zero, while the refusal owner prints its reason exactly once.

### Post-rebase fixture correction

The first focused run after rebasing failed because merged #109832 correctly archived the old fixture's older sidecar row; the child then continued to a locally occupied gateway port. That was a stale test premise, not a product regression. The fixture now uses a newer divergent sidecar timestamp, which is the migration state that must remain unresolved. The corrected exact-head run is green.

Mandatory uncommitted autoreview of that fixture correction reported:

```text
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.98)
```

### Pre-fix contrast and native-crash boundary

An earlier run from pre-fix merge base `433b3ce86d71a88fb34d4f61f6f10c36b912aeee` exited status 1 with no signal on this host, but included `generic_wrapper_count=1`; the patched path has `generic_wrapper_count=0`. The reporter's SIGSEGV did not reproduce in this environment on either revision. This proof establishes the clean typed-exit contract owned by this PR; identifying the reporter's crashing native module remains deferred pending their core dump.

### Verification

```text
pnpm format src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts
Finished in 4ms on 1 files using 1 threads.

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.state-migration.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       24 passed (24)
Duration    2.51s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 4.62s

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
passed
```

## What Was Not Tested

- The reporter's exact container/supervisor/native-module failure was not reproduced; identifying the crashing native module requires the reporter's core dump and is intentionally deferred.
- No successful full gateway channel/provider startup was exercised. The real child process stops at the intended preflight refusal, before `runGatewayCommand` starts runtime services.
- No broad suite was run; focused coverage exercises the changed refusal owner, existing migration cases, child-process exit semantics, lease cleanup, and the scoped core changed gate.

target.title: feat(sessions): raise default session-store disk budget to 10 GiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The per-agent session-store disk budget defaults to 2 GiB. For a long-lived personal agent with a rolling main session, that budget is the only bound on archived transcript retention — and 2 GiB starts evicting conversation history far too early. Archives are the agent's long-term conversational record; evicting them is silent memory loss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Raise the default `session.maintenance.maxDiskBytes` from 2 GiB to 10 GiB. Disk is cheap; conversation history is not recoverable. The high-water mark stays at the derived 80% (now 8 GiB). Operators on constrained disks can still set a lower budget or `false` to disable.

## User Impact

Agents keep roughly 5× more archived transcript history before oldest-first eviction kicks in. No config migration needed — explicit `maxDiskBytes` values are untouched; only the unset default changes.

## Evidence

- `src/config/sessions/store-maintenance.ts` — `DEFAULT_SESSION_MAX_DISK_BYTES` 2 GiB → 10 GiB

target.title: fix(discord): honor caller abortSignal during 429 retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`requestDiscord` in `extensions/discord/src/api.ts` retries 429 responses with a backoff driven by `retryAsync`. The caller's `options.signal` is honored by the fetch itself (merged into the per-attempt request signal), but the sleep between attempts used the default unabortable timer. With `retry_after` up to 60s (and `maxDelayMs` at 5 minutes), an aborted caller still waited out the full backoff and then issued one more request whose result would be discarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

`retryAsync` accepts a custom `sleep`; this passes `sleepWithAbort(ms, options?.signal)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` — the same abort-aware helper adopted for retry backoffs in sibling fixes (#109604 telegram startup probe, #108561 discord gateway READY retry, #108408 feishu comment reply retry). When the signal fires mid-backoff, the sleep's abort rejection propagates through `retryAsync` and rejects `requestDiscord` immediately, mirroring how an abort during the fetch itself surfaces. Without a signal, `sleepWithAbort` degenerates to a plain ref'd timer, so existing callers that pass no `signal` see zero behavior change.

## Changes

- Pass an abort-aware `sleep` to `retryAsync` in `requestDiscord`, wired to `options.signal`.
- Add a regression test: a real loopback HTTP server that counts requests and always returns 429 with `retry_after: 30`, an abort fired 200ms into the backoff; asserts the request rejects promptly with an abort error and the fetcher is called exactly once.

## User Impact

Callers that cancel Discord API work (plugin shutdown, gateway teardown, aborted operations) now stop promptly during 429 rate-limit backoffs instead of sleeping up to the full `retry_after`/cap and issuing a doomed extra request.

## Evidence

Exact head: `c6080c626be8c0b4bbfc286be079ea398ab9be5d`.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/api.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  18 passed (18)
```

Same focused suite with the change stashed: the new test waits out two full 30s backoffs (`tests 63.72s`) and fails the promptness assertion. With the fix it rejects ~200ms after the abort fires.

`oxlint` clean on both changed files; `tsgo` extensions test project reports no errors in discord files.

## Intentionally out of scope

- `timeoutMs` remains a per-attempt request timeout and intentionally does not bound backoff sleeps; the caller signal is the cancellation path.
- No change to retry counts, delay caps, or Retry-After honoring.

target.title: fix(gateway): stop reporting user cancellations as gateway draining

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators stopping an async CLI agent turn would receive `timeoutPhase: gateway_draining` even though the Gateway remained healthy. The affected turn was also recorded as timed out instead of cancelled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now preserves the abort owner: operator RPC cancellation records a cancelled task without a timeout phase, maintenance expiry remains timed out, and restart cancellation alone carries the gateway-draining phase. The existing wire-level `status: timeout` response remains unchanged for compatibility.

## User Impact

Operators and automation can distinguish a deliberate Stop action from Gateway shutdown or maintenance timeout. Control UI still ends the turn as Cancelled/Interrupted, while CLI task history now reports the matching cancellation state.

target.title: fix(slack): keep draft previews with custom identity
target.body:
Closes #107861

Disclosure: AI was used to understand the codebase and review the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Slack users with a custom outbound username or icon would lose portable draft-preview streaming when native streaming transport was disabled. Long-running top-level DM requests showed lifecycle reactions but no live preview, even though final replies still arrived.

## Why This Change Was Made

Portable draft selection now follows the configured streaming mode regardless of custom identity, but the temporary draft preview stays disposable by using the app identity. The final delivery path applies the configured custom Slack identity, so cleanup does not depend on deleting a custom-identity message.

## User Impact

Slack users can keep custom agent names and avatars while receiving live draft and tool-progress previews in configurations that use portable streaming. No configuration or migration changes are required.

## Evidence

- Added dispatch regressions covering disposable portable draft previews followed by custom-identity final delivery for text and media replies.
- Verified the custom-identity path does not use final preview edit/finalize behavior, clears the disposable draft preview, and sends the final reply with the resolved custom identity.
- Existing real Slack video proof remains attached on the PR and was accepted by ClawSweeper as `proof: sufficient` / `proof: video`.
- Follow-up reviewer concern addressed: custom-identity Slack messages are no longer used as the disposable draft preview message.

target.title: fix: keep the global loop breaker reachable after tool blocks
target.body:
Closes #109435

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agent runs repeatedly issuing the same blocked tool call could never reach the configured global circuit breaker after critical loop blocking began. Critical tool-loop vetoes were excluded from no-progress accounting, freezing the streak below the higher global threshold.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tool-loop vetoes are recorded as an explicit no-progress outcome and counted toward the current unchanged-result streak. A later changed result resets earlier vetoes so recovered runs are not stopped prematurely. Policy, approval, abort, and other blocked outcomes remain distinct, and run-termination policy remains out of scope.

## User Impact

Repeated blocked tool calls now continue through the configured escalation path, allowing the global circuit breaker to trigger at its threshold. If a tool later makes progress, vetoes from the older stalled segment no longer count against the recovered run.

## Evidence

The production `detectToolCallLoop`, `recordToolCall`, and `recordToolCallOutcome` path was exercised against a real `SessionState` with 20 identical no-progress results followed by ten tool-loop vetoes.

Before the patch, the regression remains at `generic_repeat` because vetoes do not advance the streak. After the patch, the same sequence advances from 20 through 30 and reaches the global breaker on the tenth veto:

```console
[agents/loop-detection] Critical generic loop detected: read repeated 20 times
after-real-outcomes=generic_repeat:20
[agents/loop-detection] Critical generic loop detected: read repeated 21 times
after-veto-1=generic_repeat:21
[agents/loop-detection] Critical generic loop detected: read repeated 29 times
after-veto-9=generic_repeat:29
after-veto-10=global_circuit_breaker:30
[agents/loop-detection] Global circuit breaker triggered: read repeated 30 times with no progress
```

Validation completed:

```console
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts
# 58 detector tests and 84 end-to-end tests passed

pnpm check:test-types
# passed all core, extension, and root test typechecks

./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts src/logging/diagnostic-session-state.ts
./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts src/logging/diagnostic-session-state.ts
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
# passed
```

The changed-result regression additionally verifies that progress resets older vetoes, so a recovered run does not inherit the stalled segment's count. The changed-file gate reached a repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline failure that reproduces on clean `origin/main`; this PR does not touch that surface.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: tool-loop vetoes froze the no-progress streak after critical blocking, making the global circuit breaker unreachable.
- Real environment tested: macOS with Node 24.16, exercising the production loop-detection module against a real `SessionState`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: a `node --import tsx --input-type=module` probe imported `detectToolCallLoop`, `recordToolCall`, and `recordToolCallOutcome`, recorded 20 identical results, then recorded ten `loop-veto` outcomes while printing each detector verdict.
- Evidence after fix: the copied terminal output above shows streak 20 after real outcomes, 21 after the first veto, 29 after the ninth veto, and `global_circuit_breaker:30` after the tenth veto.
- Observed result after fix: the global breaker becomes reachable while critical blocking remains sticky before the final threshold.
- What was not tested: a full provider-backed agent turn running until the breaker; the production-function probe covers the exact detector and session-state path repaired here.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: actual run termination remains intentionally out of scope for this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu DM users received a misleading "reply completed without visible content" warning when an agent intentionally returned `NO_REPLY` through the message-end block-reply path.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users sending direct messages could receive no agent reply when Feishu rejected delivery to the sender's `open_id` with error 230101.

Inbound replies now use the conversation `chat_id` supplied by Feishu while sender-scoped identity, policy, session routing, and proactive user-targeted sends remain unchanged. Synthetic menu and card-action events without a real Feishu conversation ID keep the existing sender-targeted fallback.

## User Impact

Feishu direct-message replies can be delivered through the existing conversation instead of being lost after the agent completes its response. Text, card, media, and streaming replies share this dispatcher target.

## Evidence

- Before: the issue reporter reproduced error 230101 when sending the DM reply with `receive_id_type=open_id`, while the same reply succeeded with the inbound conversation `chat_id`.
- A focused regression failed before the fix because the DM reply dispatcher received `user:ou_sender_1`; it passes after the fix with `chat:oc_dm`, while last-route state remains `user:ou_sender_1`.

- Targeted formatting, lint, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- A live Feishu tenant was not available locally. Live after-fix delivery remains to be confirmed by a reviewer with Feishu credentials; the issue's live API A/B result and the focused dispatcher-target regression provide the available proof.

- Real environment tested: the reporter's Feishu tenant supplied the before-fix API result; this branch was validated locally against the production inbound-routing and dispatcher paths.

target.title: fix(release): stabilize frozen validation tools
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Canonical Full Release Validation https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29618658630 reached candidate-owned CI and release children, exposing two deterministic frozen-tooling mismatches:

- macOS CI job https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29618679716/job/88009169925 installed today's Homebrew SwiftFormat and rejected 118 unchanged v6.11-era Swift files;
- no-write Docker image jobs attempted local `--load` while retaining SBOM/provenance attestations, which Docker's local exporter rejects as manifest lists.

No product test failed. Both failures are validation tool contracts that drifted from the frozen source tree.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. Pin the reviewed v6.11 formatter contract: SwiftFormat `0.61.1`, archive SHA-256 `b990400779aceb7d7020796eb9ba814d4480543f671d38fc0ff48cb72f04c584`. This adapts #104728 (`7772d798dd67c96a3e2d13d8dedc3d42c98bcc46`), #104740 (`ce671c3513769b10877e6181dfc7f6b48cf86e05`), and bounded download work #108685 (`e0394c2ab43133978b7452e96dea715a6efdbd3b`).
2. Disable SBOM/provenance only for validation-owned local image loads, matching #103891 (`69f8198ba3d31d6a83b39b837e7f97a0ea0f1885`). Docker cannot load attestation manifest lists into the local engine; the resulting image bytes are still packed and integrity-bound as immutable workflow artifacts.

The alternatives—reformatting 118 native files or restoring registry-published validation images—would import broad native churn or reintroduce publication permissions into this npm-only extended-stable release.

## User Impact

No runtime, package, dependency, version, or native behavior changes. Candidate validation becomes reproducible and remains no-write.

Release scope remains `v2026.6.33`, npm `extended-stable`, core plus the canonical `all-publishable` official plugin inventory at exact version `2026.6.33`. No tag or publication has occurred; Docker/native/GitHub Release/ClawHub/mobile/website publication remains excluded.

Security: the official SwiftFormat archive is fail-closed against an exact SHA-256 and bounded by connection/total/retry timeouts. Registry-published images retain attestations outside this validation-only path; local validation images remain content-bound by artifact digest and archive SHA-256.

## Evidence

- Parent failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29618658630
- SwiftFormat failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29618679716/job/88009169925
- Local-load failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29618681467/job/88009435210
- Live SwiftFormat archive checksum: `b990400779aceb7d7020796eb9ba814d4480543f671d38fc0ff48cb72f04c584`
- `actionlint` on both touched workflows: pass
- Six focused release/workflow suites: 115/115 pass
- Changed-test oxfmt: pass
- `git diff --check`: pass

After merge, npm preflight and Full Release Validation will be rerun from the canonical branch at its new exact head. No historical evidence will be reused.

target.title: fix(memory): recover from same-file legacy index divergence
target.body:
Related: #108532

Continues #109865. This supersedes that stalled PR because its contributor branch cannot be updated from this environment. Credit to @Serhii-Leniv for the original fix; the first three commits preserve Serhii Leniv's authorship.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with legacy and canonical Memory Core rows in the same per-agent SQLite database could enter a Gateway crash loop when rows shared an identity but held different values. In this state, `openclaw doctor --fix` could report success without repairing the database, and the next Gateway start failed again.

The original report is closed as #108532, but its [Docker reproduction and doctor evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108532#issuecomment-4987458050) show the same-file failure remained: the mounted `main.sqlite` kept conflicting after doctor ran and the Gateway still refused to start. This PR preserves that paper trail without reopening the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Summary

Same-file migration now treats existing canonical rows as authoritative, imports non-conflicting legacy-only rows, and drops the legacy tables only after proving every eligible identity is represented canonically. Chunk migration snapshots ownership before copying so stale chunks cannot be mixed into a source that already has a canonical chunk set. A partially migrated, chunkless source imports legacy chunks only when its source metadata still matches; divergent source metadata is removed so normal source sync must rebuild current content instead of accepting stale chunks.

The original migration tests were split into `memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts`, keeping both test files below the max-lines limit without a lint suppression or loss of migration-boundary coverage.

### Root Cause

On current `main`, the same-file migration's copied-row assertion compares full row values. When canonical and legacy `meta`, `files`, `chunks`, or `embedding_cache` rows have the same key but different values, it throws a plain `Error("legacy memory <table> rows conflict with canonical memory index rows")`.

That path is reached by Memory Core schema initialization during runtime startup and by doctor before doctor enters the sidecar-import recovery block. The recovery added in #108652 catches `LegacyMemoryDerivedRowsConflictError` from the sidecar import only, so it cannot recover this plain same-file error. The result matches #108532's observed Docker behavior: startup repeatedly fails while doctor leaves the same conflict in place.

This change uses SQLite's conflict-ignore behavior only for duplicate canonical identities, then verifies identity/source ownership explicitly before dropping legacy tables. Rows that cannot be represented by the canonical STRICT schema still fail closed and retain the legacy tables.

## User Impact

Memory Core can start again when an older same-file index contains stale values for keys already present in the canonical tables. Canonical indexed content wins, safe legacy-only content is retained, and repeating schema initialization is idempotent.

Genuinely uncopyable legacy rows—for example, values rejected by canonical STRICT constraints—still hard-fail. That residual recovery case is intentionally unchanged and remains follow-up work rather than being silently discarded here.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Proof environment: Linux source checkout, Node `v25.9.0`, real on-disk `DatabaseSync` files in WAL mode. The current-main baseline was `a9dc393f7eb84f515994789b8eefafa206e96914`; the patched head was `c0e42f72d35c99e4e08aa1b115e88ca77a5a1fb5`.

Each run began from an independently seeded state directory. The affected database lived at its real canonical path, `<state>/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`. target.title: fix(memory): bound qmd taskkill cleanup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QMD timeout, abort, and availability cleanup used synchronous `taskkill.exe` calls on Windows. A stalled system utility could block the Node event loop after the QMD operation had already reached its own deadline, delaying command settlement and gateway work indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows process-tree cleanup now launches `taskkill.exe` asynchronously and settles its cleanup attempt after five seconds without waiting for the utility to exit. The timed-out helper is terminated and detached, while the retained QMD child handle remains the final fallback.

The cleanup also rechecks the QMD child's authoritative `exitCode` and `signalCode` before forced escalation or direct kill. This avoids retrying a reusable PID after QMD exits while the asynchronous taskkill attempt is in flight. A timeout result is fixed before `kill()` runs so a synchronous child-process error cannot incorrectly trigger a second `/F` attempt.

## User Impact

On Windows, QMD operations now settle at their own timeout or abort deadline even if `taskkill.exe` stalls, so cleanup no longer blocks the gateway event loop. Normal graceful-to-forced tree cleanup remains intact for fast failures, and exited QMD processes are not targeted again by PID.

## Evidence

- Node 24.15.0: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.test.ts` (27/27 passed)
- Node 24.15.0: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.real.test.ts` (2/2 passed)
- Regression coverage verifies heartbeat responsiveness during a stalled taskkill, five-second helper settlement, retained-handle fallback, synchronous kill errors, late taskkill events, and QMD exit before retry
- `oxfmt --check packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.test.ts`
- Targeted `oxlint` on both changed files

- Node 24 child-process source/types and Bun child-process compatibility were inspected for `spawn`, exit state, `kill`, and `unref` behavior

Proof gap: no Windows machine capable of deliberately stalling `taskkill.exe` was available in this session. The focused tests exercise the exact asynchronous OpenClaw path and event-loop behavior; GitHub CI remains the clean-environment gate.

target.title: fix: keep broken SSH sandbox refs agent-scoped
target.body:
Related: #101265

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with one broken SSH sandbox SecretRef could lose Gateway startup or unrelated agent sandboxing, while an unresolved direct SSH identity could fall through to ambient filesystem or agent configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sandbox secret collection now assigns exact normalized agent owners, duplicates inherited defaults only for relevant agents, and ignores unrelated per-agent overrides in shared scope. Sandbox resolution and SSH manager paths validate the effective agent owner plus the selected raw SSH refs before filesystem or network access, returning the existing typed unavailable error for only that agent. SSH lifecycle credentials remain materialized while SSH is configured, so disabling an agent or sandbox does not strand inspection or removal of an existing remote runtime.

No config, environment, UI, protocol, or capability surface is added.

## User Impact

The Gateway continues starting when one agent has a broken SSH sandbox secret. That agent's sandbox stays cold, while healthy agents remain available. Broken direct SSH secret refs cannot silently fall through to another profile or ambient identity. Existing SSH runtimes remain manageable after sandbox deactivation.

target.title: fix(auth): decouple plugin synthetic-auth from profile fallback for gateway attempts (#110103)
target.body:
Closes #110103

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where anthropic-vertex users whose only credential is Google ADC (Application Default Credentials) hit "No API key found" on gateway-routed model calls, even though the same synthetic ADC auth resolves under `--local` and the plugin itself confirms it works.

## Why This Change Was Made

A gateway direct-attempt sets `allowAuthProfileFallback: false` so an unrelated stored-profile store cannot replace or pre-reject the immutable env/config source. `resolveApiKeyForProvider` was gating the provider plugin synthetic-auth hook on that same flag (`allowPluginSyntheticAuth: params.allowAuthProfileFallback !== false`), so turning off profile fallback also silenced the plugin hook and the gateway path failed for ADC-only providers.

This adds a distinct `allowPluginSyntheticAuth` flag on `resolveApiKeyForProvider` and `getApiKeyForModel`. It defaults to the previous coupled value so existing callers are unchanged, and the two gateway direct-attempt seams (`runtime-plan/resolve-auth` and the embedded-agent-runner `auth-controller`) pass it `true`. Stored-profile discovery stays gated by `allowAuthProfileFallback`, so the prepared-attempt isolation invariant is preserved: enabling plugin synthetic-auth does not re-open the profile store.

## User Impact

anthropic-vertex and other GCP-ADC-only providers now authenticate over the gateway route the same way they already do under `--local`. No behavior change for any provider that resolves through a stored profile or an env/config key.

## Evidence

Two regression tests added in `src/agents/model-auth.test.ts`:
- a gateway-isolated attempt (`allowAuthProfileFallback: false`) now resolves plugin synthetic auth
- stored-profile isolation still holds: a stored api-key profile stays unresolved when profile fallback is off, even with `allowPluginSyntheticAuth: true`

```

```

target.title: fix(memory): bound qmd taskkill cleanup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QMD timeout, abort, and availability cleanup used synchronous `taskkill.exe` calls on Windows. A stalled system utility could block the Node event loop after the QMD operation had already reached its own deadline, delaying command settlement and gateway work indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows process-tree cleanup now launches `taskkill.exe` asynchronously and settles its cleanup attempt after five seconds without waiting for the utility to exit. The timed-out helper is terminated and detached, while the retained QMD child handle remains the final fallback.

The cleanup also rechecks the QMD child's authoritative `exitCode` and `signalCode` before forced escalation or direct kill. This avoids retrying a reusable PID after QMD exits while the asynchronous taskkill attempt is in flight. A timeout result is fixed before `kill()` runs so a synchronous child-process error cannot incorrectly trigger a second `/F` attempt.

## User Impact

On Windows, QMD operations now settle at their own timeout or abort deadline even if `taskkill.exe` stalls, so cleanup no longer blocks the gateway event loop. Normal graceful-to-forced tree cleanup remains intact for fast failures, and exited QMD processes are not targeted again by PID.

## Evidence

- Node 24.15.0: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.test.ts` (27/27 passed)
- Node 24.15.0: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.real.test.ts` (2/2 passed)
- Regression coverage verifies heartbeat responsiveness during a stalled taskkill, five-second helper settlement, retained-handle fallback, synchronous kill errors, late taskkill events, and QMD exit before retry
- `oxfmt --check packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.test.ts`
- Targeted `oxlint` on both changed files
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- Node 24 child-process source/types and Bun child-process compatibility were inspected for `spawn`, exit state, `kill`, and `unref` behavior
- Two-pass independent adversarial review found and then cleared the timeout-result and stale-PID races; the final code review had no actionable finding

Proof gap: no Windows machine capable of deliberately stalling `taskkill.exe` was available in this session. The focused tests exercise the exact asynchronous OpenClaw path and event-loop behavior; GitHub CI remains the clean-environment gate.

target.title: fix: pre-beta.2 state DB upgrade wedges gateway startup and doctor --fix
target.body:
Closes #109867

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users upgrading from `2026.7.2-beta.1` (or any pre-beta.2 state database) would have the gateway fail to start and `openclaw doctor --fix` fail during the shared-state schema migration, leaving the service stranded (reported on macOS LaunchAgent and independently reproduced on Ubuntu systemd in the issue thread).

The failing step is the additive migration for `managed_outgoing_image_records`: it adds `original_media_root` as `TEXT NOT NULL` with no `DEFAULT`. SQLite rejects that `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` whenever the table has rows — and on older SQLite builds (within OpenClaw's supported Node floor) even when it is empty — so both the startup `ensureSchema` path and the doctor repair path abort with `Cannot add a NOT NULL column with default value NULL`, before the beta.2 index DDL is ever reached.

## Why This Change Was Made

The additive DDL becomes `original_media_root TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, which is executable on every supported SQLite build regardless of table contents, plus the matching `allowedColumnDefinitions` entry in the maintenance schema-compatibility map — the same pattern already used for `current_conversation_bindings.target_agent_id`, whose additive DDL likewise carries a `DEFAULT` the canonical schema omits. The canonical STRICT-table rebuild still normalizes the final shape for databases below the current schema version; no schema-version bump is involved. The empty-string backfill only ever applies to rows written before the column existed (the table had no shipped writer then), and `record_json` remains the durable full record.

## User Impact

Upgrades from pre-beta.2 state databases now complete: the gateway starts normally and `doctor --fix` repairs the schema instead of wedging. Existing rows survive with the new columns backfilled. No behavior change for databases already on the current shape.

## Evidence

Focused test lanes (all green):

```
pnpm test src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts
 Tests  80 passed | 1 skipped (81)
pnpm test src/infra/sqlite-schema-contract.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.permissions.test.ts
 [test] passed 2 Vitest shards
```

New regression tests build a real state DB, strip it to the pre-beta.2 15-column shape (drop the two agent indexes + three columns), insert a legacy row, then drive both the normal startup open and `repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema()` — asserting the columns are restored, the legacy row survives, and `original_media_root` backfills to `''`.

A 5-case before/after matrix was also driven through the real production functions on pristine `origin/main` vs. this branch, scored by an external QC harness (Synthia anchor-check panel — objective pass/fail only):

```
  [PASS] main-repro/doctor-repair-legacy-with-row     main wedges with 'Cannot add a NOT NULL column with default value NULL'
  [PASS] main-repro/startup-open-legacy-with-row      main wedges with 'Cannot add a NOT NULL column with default value NULL'
  [PASS] after/doctor-repair-empty-legacy             upgrade succeeds, columns present
  [PASS] after/doctor-repair-legacy-with-row          upgrade succeeds, columns present, legacy row survives
  [PASS] after/startup-open-legacy                    upgrade succeeds, columns present
  [PASS] after/startup-open-legacy-with-row           upgrade succeeds, columns present
  [PASS] after/repair-idempotent-on-current           upgrade succeeds, columns present

Synthia QC panel: 8/8 checks passed, anchor fidelity 100.0
```

Note on the empty-table cases: they pass on main under Node 26's bundled SQLite (which permits the NOT NULL ALTER on empty tables), which is why the matrix's main-repro anchors are the populated-table cases; on older supported SQLite builds the empty-table path fails on main too — matching the issue's original empty-table report.

To rule out latent failure modes beyond the hand-picked cases, a seeded randomized upgrade matrix (48 scenarios, seed 109867, reproducible) was also driven through the real production functions: all 7 partial-column states a manual recovery can leave behind (any subset of `agent_id`/`original_media_root`/`cleanup_pending` missing) × both upgrade paths, pre-STRICT `user_version=2` databases, 0–25 rows including unicode/quote/2KB-string contents, plus doctor double-run idempotency:

```
fix branch:  48/48 scenarios upgrade cleanly (columns restored, rows survive, backfill '')
origin/main: 26/48 — all 22 failures are exactly the fixed class
             (original_media_root missing + populated table); no other failure mode
             surfaced, and no scenario passing on main regresses on this branch
```

**Real `doctor --fix` behavior proof** (source checkout via `pnpm openclaw`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, scratch paths redacted). Fixture: a real state database created by the production schema code, stripped to the pre-beta.2 15-column `managed_outgoing_image_records` shape with one legacy row inserted — the same reconstruction the issue's reporters describe:

$ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive

│ - Failed migrating shared state database schema at
│   <state-dir>/state/openclaw.sqlite:
│   Error: Cannot add a NOT NULL column with default value NULL
│ Failed detecting Reef identity keys: PluginStateStoreError: ...

    "SELECT attachment_id, quote(original_media_root), cleanup_pending FROM managed_outgoing_image_records;"

target.title: fix(google-meet): harden talkback bridge recovery
target.body:
Related: #109755, #110089

## What Problem This Solves

PR #110089 landed the three deferred meeting-bot findings while this branch was completing exact-head proof. Sibling-path review found two remaining Google Meet bridge hazards: paired-node talkback could start while microphone state was unknown, and delayed bridge recovery could select another node or open a second tab when tab reuse was disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser-managed local and paired-node talkback now require an explicit `micMuted: false` observation before realtime audio starts. The explicit externally managed `chrome.launch: false` contract remains unchanged and is documented at its early-return boundary. Delayed bridge recovery pins the session's node and forces the existing-session `chrome.launch: false` path, so it attaches audio without navigating or opening another tab.

## User Impact

Google Meet bots no longer start realtime audio from an unknown microphone state. A paired-node session that becomes speech-ready later keeps its original node and tracked call tab.

## Evidence

- 160 Google Meet integration tests pass, including local and paired-node muted, unknown, unmuted, externally managed, and post-unmute recovery paths.
- 7 Chrome transport tests pass.
- The recovery regression uses `reuseExistingTab: false` and proves `/tabs/open` occurs exactly once.
- Targeted Google Meet lint and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh final-delta autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings, patch correct at 0.99 confidence.
- Final exact-head release gate passed all 134 jobs at `b7530205a6ff`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29618128276.

## Maintainer Decision

Unknown microphone state is fail-closed for browser-managed talkback. It remains transiently blocked until Meet explicitly reports `micMuted: false`. Explicit `chrome.launch: false` is the externally managed exception: the external owner supplies the already-open call, so browser health is unavailable and configuring this mode authorizes its bridge directly.

Live signed-in Meet/audio validation was unavailable: connected nodes do not expose the `google-meet` capability, and the approved Meet-capable node is offline. The browser-facing contracts are covered by focused integration tests.

target.title: Add experimental Claw lifecycle diagnostics
target.body:
## Summary

- add an experimental core doctor check that projects the canonical Claw lifecycle status model into structured health findings
- report partial installs, missing or modified agents, workspace drift, package drift/incomplete state, MCP ownership drift, unresolved cron ownership, and orphaned subordinate rows
- preserve source MCP placeholders while inspecting runtime config so resolved credentials cannot create false drift
- keep the check and ordered doctor contribution absent unless `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`

## Contract

- doctor reuses `claws status` ownership states instead of independently interpreting managed resources
- absent and pre-Claws state produce no findings and no state directory, database, schema, migration, chmod, checkpoint, or journal-mode change
- existing state is observed through one read-only handle; missing experimental ownership tables are treated as empty only in read-only mode
- unreadable, invalid, or forward-version state databases return one structured error finding rather than aborting doctor
- source MCP config is read through the canonical source-config API; `${ENV_VAR}` placeholders remain unexpanded
- diagnostics are advisory and do not mutate config, files, scheduler state, provenance, database bytes, metadata, schema, or journal mode

## Verification

- test-source typecheck
- focused Oxlint: 0 warnings and 0 errors
- formatting and `git diff --check`
- 183 focused lifecycle, collector, shared-state, core-check, and doctor-contribution tests
- absent/pre-Claws tests prove doctor creates no state and changes no bytes
- existing-state test compares database bytes, mtime, mode, `sqlite_master`, `user_version`, and `journal_mode` before and after doctor
- invalid and newer-schema tests prove open failures become structured findings and handles close cleanly
- full Codex review against #102406: no actionable findings

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102406 MCP ownership
- This PR: read-only lifecycle and drift diagnostics
- Next: #102959 uses the same ownership model for grouped update planning

Doctor lands after every add/remove owner so it can reuse one authoritative status model instead of inventing partial resource checks. The Claws CLI and doctor surface remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

target.title: fix: bound gateway model pricing cache
target.body:
Closes #101543.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running gateway processes could keep growing the model-pricing cache when refreshes see many dynamic provider/plugin model rows, eventually increasing heap pressure and risking OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cache is capped at the shared gateway pricing state boundary so every refresh replacement path is bounded consistently. Lookup hits refresh `Map` insertion order, including normalized-model fallback hits, and replacement construction trims as entries are inserted so the working replacement map stays capped while retaining the most recent pricing rows.

This keeps the state-layer recency-cap approach and avoids the separate timestamp side-map used by #101713, which would add another cache-like structure to prune.

## User Impact

Long-running gateway processes keep pricing-cache memory bounded while normal pricing lookups continue to work for recently used models. Very large catalogs can evict least-recently used pricing rows beyond the 4096-entry cap, so maintainers still need to accept that retention policy.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: the shared gateway pricing state boundary caps replacement payloads at 4096 entries, evicts oldest rows during construction, preserves direct lookup hits, and preserves normalized lookup hits across an over-limit refresh.
- Current branch head: `3c2b18dd759379d6e8fcacce89a0c2d1f519f2c8`.
- Source path checked: `refreshGatewayModelPricingCache` calls `replaceGatewayModelPricingCache` for both seeded-only and full refresh maps, so the state-boundary cap covers the real refresh replacement path.
- Focused proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/model-pricing-cache.test.ts` -> passed 1 test file / 25 tests on the current head.
- Focused regression coverage in `src/gateway/model-pricing-cache.test.ts` verifies over-limit replacement caps size and evicts oldest rows, recently used direct lookup rows survive an over-limit refresh, and normalized lookup hits refresh recency and survive an over-limit refresh.

target.title: fix(gateway): serialize same-session agent hook dispatches to stop claim-race drops
target.body:
Closes #110109

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators sending multiple near-simultaneous `/hooks/agent` events for the same session (for example a webhook burst: review + inline comments) would silently lose later events when `cron.maxConcurrentRuns > 1`. The first run claimed the session lifecycle lock; losers threw `CronSessionLifecycleClaimError` with no retry, so legitimate automation wakes never ran.

## Why This Change Was Made

Serialize agent-hook runs **per resolved `sessionKey`** at the gateway dispatch boundary: later same-session dispatches chain behind the in-flight run (FIFO), while different session keys stay concurrent. Isolated-agent module load is memoized so concurrent dispatches share one import. This matches the durable fix shape (session-owned queue at hook dispatch) rather than blind pattern retries that can replay side effects after work has started.

Compatibility: no config, protocol, or public API change — only in-process ordering of detached hook work. Performance: different sessions still overlap; idle per-session chains are deleted after the last run. Usability: previously dropped wakes are retained in order. Security: no trust-boundary change; still runs through the existing hook sanitize and system-event paths.

## User Impact

Same-session hook bursts complete in arrival order instead of silently discarding losers. Cross-session concurrency and existing single-hook behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass).

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server/hooks.agent-serialization.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server/hooks.agent-trust.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts
# Test Files  3 passed (3)
# Tests  40 passed (40)

# Dispatch-level serialization (hooks.agent-serialization.test.ts):
# - queues a same-session burst so the second wake is never dropped
# - processes a same-session burst strictly in arrival order
# - does not serialize hooks targeting different session keys
# - keeps draining the session queue after a run fails

# Live Gateway HTTP burst (server.hooks.test.ts, withGatewayServer):
# - cold concurrent first-request same-session POST /hooks/agent burst
# - second same-session isolated run starts only after the first releases
# - second payload message preserved as "inline comment" (FIFO)
# - concurrent cross-session POSTs both start before either finishes
# Full server.hooks suite: 26/26 passed including the new burst case

# Follow-up code: process-wide agentHookRunChains Map (module scope) so lazy
# concurrent first-request handler init cannot split same-session serialization

# Static (closeout):
# oxfmt on touched files: pass
# git diff --check: pass
```

Head: `5b880417e4`

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Concurrent same-session `/hooks/agent` dispatches no longer race the cron session-lifecycle claim and drop loser payloads; they run FIFO for one `sessionKey` while other keys stay concurrent. The session queue is process-wide (module scope), so a cold concurrent first-request burst on a running Gateway still serializes correctly even if lazy handler creation races.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout; live Gateway via `withGatewayServer` (real HTTP listener + hooks request path) with mocked `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` so isolated turns block/release under test control without a paid model call.
- Current-main contrast: On main, each dispatch immediately starts an independent root-work continuation, so two same-session runs can both enter `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` and compete for the lifecycle claim; the loser surfaces only as `Hook (error): Session … changed while starting work. Retry.` with no retry owner.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/gateway/server/hooks.agent-serialization.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts -t "serializes same-session"
  ```
  Live Gateway case (no warmup): Promise.all of two same-session POST `/hooks/agent` with deferred first run; assert second isolated run is not called until first releases; assert second message is `inline comment`; then two different session keys both start before either finishes.
- Evidence after fix: dispatch serialization 4/4 + live Gateway burst 1/1 + full `server.hooks.test.ts` 26/26 + agent-trust 10/10 (40 total across the three files). Second same-session HTTP wake starts only after the first release; cross-session overlap retained.
- Control check: cross-session concurrency case proves serialization is keyed by `sessionKey` only; agent-trust suite still covers admission retention, non-ok announce, and detached work behavior on the same dispatch surface.
- Observed result after fix: same-session HTTP bursts queue and complete in arrival order with no dropped second wake on a cold Gateway; different sessions still run in parallel; queue continues after a failed run (dispatch-level case).
- What was not tested: live multi-process Gateway HTTP POST burst against a full agent/model turn; end-to-end cron scheduler ownership for non-hook jobs (unchanged).

## AI disclosure

target.title: fix(mac): open the receiving agent's conversation from Quick Chat under global scope
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes the known limitation shipped in #109952: after Quick Chat sends to a non-default agent under **global** session scope, Command-Return opened the unqualified `global` WebChat — the default agent's conversation — because the WebChat window contract had no agent discriminator (`chat.send` permits a separate `agentId` only for global routing, and each agent owns its own `global` store).

## Why This Change Was Made

Minimal threading through existing seams — the shared chat UI already supports per-agent global routing (`MacGatewayChatTransport(defaultGlobalAgentID:)`, `initialActiveAgentID:`); only the macOS plumbing dropped it:

- `WebChatRoute` (session key + normalized agent id) replaces string tracking in `WebChatManager`; window/panel reuse compares the full route, and session-key callbacks retain the explicit agent while guarding against stale controllers (fixing a latent stale-callback clobber in the process).
- `WebChatSwiftUIWindowController` gains an optional `agentID`; an explicit selection feeds the existing transport/view-model seams and is pinned against gateway-default refreshes (`explicitAgentID ?? latestDefaultAgentID`).
- `AppNavigationActions.openChat(sessionKey:agentID:)` is route-aware with unchanged no-arg behavior; Quick Chat's Command-Return now opens the accepted route's conversation — global scope included — and the v2 tradeoff comment is retired.

## User Impact

Command-Return after a Quick Chat send always lands in the conversation that received the message, for any agent and any session scope. All existing entry points behave exactly as before (nil agent = today's default resolution; canonical `agent:<id>:…` keys ignore ambient agents by existing resolver rules).

Release-note context: `fix(mac): Quick Chat Command-Return opens the receiving agent's conversation under global session scope`.

## Evidence

- Design follows a validated code recon of the shared-UI seams (462 lines, file:line-cited); no protocol, server, or shared-kit changes.
- Structured autoreview (Codex gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): build-time pass clean; my independent pass raised one finding — manager routes going stale if the window switched agents internally — rejected with source proof: `activeAgentId` mutates only from routing-snapshot updates (ChatViewModel.swift:534), this surface has no in-window agent switcher, and explicit routes are pinned by the controller precedence; the invariant is now documented at the callback site.
- Tests: route-identity reuse (same key/different agent → fresh controller), explicit-vs-default precedence, Quick Chat navigation seam passing both route components; suites follow the established patterns.
- Local gates: release build pass, lint 0, format 0, `git diff --check` clean; `swift test` runs on the macos-swift CI lane (author machine blocked by pre-existing Xcode-beta errors in untouched files).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where interactive `openclaw setup` users with failed inference verification could be moved into local setup application and the agent TUI instead of continuing the requested conversational repair flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inference gate now calls guided onboarding with an explicit `chat` handoff. Plain `openclaw onboard` keeps its new local hatch default, while setup repair preserves its established conversational owner boundary.

## User Impact

Users who run `openclaw setup` to repair expired or broken model access return to the setup chat after guided AI recovery. The ordinary first-run onboarding hatch and remote onboarding behavior are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Interactive `openclaw setup` repair no longer inherits the local onboarding hatch after its initial inference verification fails.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, GitHub head `25a45c717f48` (tree `581152a9f446`), branch `fix/setup-repair-chat-handoff`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** A one-shot `node --import tsx --input-type=module` PTY harness launched the real `src/entry.ts setup` command with isolated HOME/state/config and a loopback OpenAI Responses-compatible provider. The provider intentionally returned HTTP 500 for the first inference probe, then a real SSE completion for guided activation. The harness waited for the actual system-agent chat surface and exited it with Ctrl-C.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of the real `node` + PTY + provider-transport run (live stdout):

  ```text
  RESULT requests=2 first_probe_failed=1 chat_surface=1 exit_code=0
  PASS interactive setup repair returned to chat
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The first configured-model probe failed, guided setup activated the same route on the next live completion, and `openclaw setup` visibly entered the `openclaw setup - openclaw local` chat with `local ready | idle` instead of launching the hatch TUI.
- **What was not tested:** The proof used an isolated loopback OpenAI Responses-compatible provider with a synthetic key, not a credential-bearing external provider. It exercised the real setup command, provider transport, failure classification, guided activation, config persistence, and final chat handoff without external credentials.
