## What Problem This Solves

The startup-migration gate refuses to report the gateway ready when a legacy `plugin-state/state.sqlite` sidecar exists whose rows are all already present in canonical shared state. Users upgrading from v2026.6.11 crash-loop because the gate treats "canonical row is newer" (legitimate live-write progression) as a conflict, leaving the sidecar in place and blocking boot.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict detection in `migrateLegacyPluginStateSidecar` compared only `value_json`/`created_at`/`expires_at` for byte equality. When a canonical row was written by a live gateway after the migration imported the sidecar data, the mismatch was always classified as a conflict — even though the canonical data was strictly newer and the sidecar held stale, redundant data.

Codex review (July 17) confirmed: the importer is still active on current main, and #102780 did not cover this plugin-state namespace. Best solution requires row-aware comparison that archives the sidecar when canonical data is strictly newer.

## User Impact

- Users upgrading from v2026.6.11 to v2026.7.1 with a legacy `plugin-state/state.sqlite` sidecar no longer crash-loop
- A redundant sidecar is automatically renamed to `.migrated` on the next startup — the sidecar data is never deleted, only retired
- The error message when a real conflict exists now reports that rows differ without claiming which copy is newer
- `openclaw doctor --fix` recovery path continues to work for the remaining (genuine) conflict case

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.15.0 (SQLite 3.51.3), branch `fix/plugin-state-sidecar-created-at-109832`, SHA `fccbafe765`

### Scenario Matrix

| Sidecar | Canonical | created_at | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{ok:true}` | `{ok:false}` | sidecar=1000, canonical=3000 | Archive (canonical newer) | ✅ |
| `{ok:true}` | `{ok:true}` | equal (1000) | Archive (values match) | ✅ |
| `{ok:true}` | `{ok:false}` | equal (1000) | **Conflict** (ambiguous) | ✅ P1 fix |
| `{ok:true}` | `{ok:false}` | sidecar=3000, canonical=1000 | **Conflict** (sidecar newer) | ✅ |
| sidecar-unique | not present | N/A | Import | ✅ |
| canonical updated, sidecar expired | expired row | canonical=3000 | Archive | ✅ |

### Test output (17 plugin-state tests, all pass)

```console
$ npx node@24.15.0 ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run doctor-state-migrations.test.ts -t "plugin-state"

 ✓ doctor-state-migrations.test.ts (92 tests | 75 skipped)
     ✓ auto-migrates the shipped plugin-state SQLite sidecar by itself
     ✓ auto-migrates the plugin-state sidecar when custom agent dirs skip session migration
     ✓ archives the plugin-state sidecar when shared state has a newer row with different value
     ✓ imports legacy-only rows and archives when remaining conflicts expired
     ✓ archives when canonical rows are newer than sidecar rows
     ✓ keeps the sidecar when the sidecar has a newer row than canonical state
     ✓ keeps the sidecar when sidecar and canonical have equal timestamps but different values
     ✓ archives the sidecar when conflicting rows already match
     ✓ lets live sidecar rows replace expired shared plugin state during migration
     ✓ archives fully covered plugin-state imports when the namespace is full

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed | 75 skipped (92)
```

### Codex Review P1 Resolution (July 17)

| Finding | Status | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `>=` silently archives divergent rows with equal timestamps | ✅ Fixed | `>=` → `>` at `plugin-state.ts:102` |
| Missing equal-timestamp divergent-value regression test | ✅ Added | `"keeps the sidecar when sidecar and canonical have equal timestamps but different values"` |

Because `legacyPluginStateRowsMatch` already verifies `value_json`, `created_at`, `expires_at` for exact equality, any row reaching the timestamp comparison has already failed field equality. Using `>=` with equal timestamps would silently discard the only recoverable sidecar copy of a divergent value. Strict `>` preserves the sidecar as a conflict in that ambiguous case.

### Exact-head brokered AWS upgrade/startup proof (July 17)

- Provider: Crabbox brokered AWS (`cbx_13cca55fabc9`, public network, no Tailscale, no hydration)
- Exact PR head: `73cf2ba0c914dc08eba27f293c0cddc33de0edb9`
- Inspectable run: [run_00dcaa1254c0](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_00dcaa1254c0)
- Trusted bootstrap verified the remote checkout SHA and confirmed the instance IAM credentials endpoint returned 404 before executing the contributor code.

```console
PRECHECK canonical={"ok":false} canonical_newer=true sidecar={"ok":true}
FIRST_START archive=present canonical={"ok":false} readyz=ok
SECOND_START archive=present migration_warning=absent readyz=ok
✓ src/commands/doctor-state-migrations.test.ts (92 tests)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       92 passed (92)
PROOF_COMPLETE exact_head=73cf2ba0c914dc08eba27f293c0cddc33de0edb9
```

The fixture created a legacy `plugin-state/state.sqlite` row with `created_at=1000` and a different, newer canonical row. The first real Gateway startup archived the sidecar to `.migrated`, preserved the canonical value, and reached `/readyz`. After a clean shutdown, the second Gateway startup reached `/readyz` without a plugin-state migration warning.

## What Changed

**`src/infra/state-migrations.plugin-state.ts`** (4 lines changed):
- `>=` → `>`: only a strictly newer canonical `created_at` triggers archival
- Error message: `"differs from shared state without a newer canonical timestamp. First key: ${key}"`

**`src/commands/doctor-state-migrations.test.ts`** (+114/-11):
- Updated 2 existing tests to expect archive (canonical newer scenarios)
- Added equal-timestamp divergent-value regression test
- Removed stale "dropped expired" assertion no longer applicable

## What Did NOT Change

- `migrateLegacyPluginStateSidecar` callers (3 call sites in `state-migrations.doctor.ts`)
- Archive logic (`.migrated` rename, WAL/shm/journal sidecar suffixes)
- `runLegacyMigrationPlans` / other channel migration paths
- Startup gate severity (warnings remain fatal — separate concern per #109073)
- Other sidecar types (task registry, flow runs, delivery queue)

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Strict `>` is the narrowest safe change. Codex review: "Change the timestamp comparison to strict > and add equal-timestamp divergent-row coverage" — both addressed.
- **Refactor needed**: No.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest-risk area**: Equal-timestamp divergent rows could theoretically be a race where canonical was written at the same millisecond as the sidecar import. In practice, this is vanishingly rare (separate SQLite databases, separate write paths). Even if it occurs, the sidecar is retained (fail-closed), and the diagnostic points to `openclaw doctor --fix`.
- **Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. The sidecar is never deleted; it is renamed to `.migrated` which is recoverable. No config, env, or schema changes.
- **Migration**: Existing `.migrated` archives from prior runs are detected and skipped at the `fileExists(sourcePath)` check.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: deepseek-v4-flash
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

target.title: fix(telegram-miniapp): cancel unread response body on auth error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Telegram Mini App page receives a non-ok HTTP response (e.g., 401 auth error), the response body stream is left dangling without being cancelled. This can leak connections and waste resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

The established codebase pattern is to cancel the response body before throwing on non-ok responses (see `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts`, `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, etc.). This fix applies the same pattern to the Telegram Mini App page handler.

The change is purely mechanical — `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` — following existing codebase convention. The body stream is unread after a non-ok response, so cancelling it is the correct cleanup action with no behavioral side effects.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Resources are cleaned up immediately on auth error instead of dangling until garbage collection.

## Test Results

All 18 tests across 7 test files pass, including the two page-specific tests and the auth-timeout simulation:


target.title: fix: deliver generated media once after image_generate completion
target.body:
Closes #108976

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram (and other channel) users received each `image_generate` result twice: once from the resumed agent reply that re-attached media, and once from the durable completion handoff that already owns delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Successful generated-media completions already set `durableGeneratedMediaHandoff` and carry `mediaUrls` / attachments for host-owned delivery. The wake instruction previously told the resumed agent to also attach every MEDIA path or structured attachment, which creates a second visible send when the agent follows that prompt.

The instruction now assigns a single media owner (the completion handoff) while preserving caption delivery on both contracts:

- message-tool-only: `message(action="send")` with a short caption and no attachments, then `NO_REPLY`
- automatic final replies: short caption text with no MEDIA lines, or `NO_REPLY`

Image, video, and music generation share this helper, so the ownership rule applies across those sibling tools without a Telegram-specific branch.

## User Impact

After `image_generate` (and sibling media tools) completes, users receive each generated artifact once, with an optional caption, instead of two identical channel deliveries a few seconds apart.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest on Windows 11 (Node v24.15.0), HEAD `5c1fa8fd86`:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/music-generate-background.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
# Tests  35 passed (35)
```

Coverage:

- shared regression asserts completion-handoff ownership, forbids MEDIA re-attach wording, and keeps message-tool caption-only guidance for message-tool-only routes
- music sibling expectations match the same shared ownership contract

Control check: wake still sets `durableGeneratedMediaHandoff: true` and still includes `mediaUrls` / attachments on the internal event for host delivery.

Live Telegram single-`sendPhoto` recording remains the user-visible acceptance gap; happy to supply a redacted log or request Mantis desktop proof after review.

Prior closed unmerged approach (#109061) forbade the message tool entirely and dropped captions on message-tool-only routes; this PR keeps caption-only `message(action="send")` while still forbidding media re-attachment.

target.title: fix(ui): show ClawHub security verdicts on first Skills load
target.body:
Fixes #108647

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening Control UI > Skills could see a clean, linked ClawHub skill labeled **Unavailable** on first load. The skill still worked, but the misleading security badge made a healthy installation look unverified.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Skills page now runs the existing verdict-only loader when it applies a route-provided status report. This hydrates security verdicts without repeating the `skills.status` request. The verdict loader follows the route's retained request-capable client even when the route snapshot is transiently `connected: false`, while preserving the existing scope/revision stale-response guards.

While the verdict request is in flight, a missing verdict is shown as **Refreshing** rather than **Unavailable**; genuine fetch errors and post-fetch missing verdicts still fail closed as **Unavailable**.

## User Impact

Linked ClawHub skills now show their real security status, such as **Clean**, on the first visit to the Skills page. There are no config, Gateway protocol, or migration changes.

## Evidence

- Real Chromium regression: `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/pages/skills/skills-page.browser.test.ts` (2 tests passed: connected route snapshot and request-capable transiently disconnected route snapshot).

- Shared Skills loader coverage: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/skills/index.test.ts` (37 tests passed).
- Final-head Control UI build passed, including sidecar and performance-budget verification.

- Final autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; patch assessed correct with 0.93 confidence.
- GitHub CI, Workflow Sanity, and all four Periphery workflows passed on the final head.

## Live Gateway Proof

Tested from commit `9f50acbe9e7b6acea7d1eaae2c12cd1d27ad6752` with a freshly built Control UI, isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`, loopback-only auth, and a real ClawHub install of `@monikazapisekstudio/socratic-dialog@0.1.3`. Tokens, ports, and local paths are redacted below.

The installed skill was eligible and linked to valid ClawHub metadata:


```console
  "schema": "openclaw.skills.security-verdicts.v1",
  "items": [{
    "ok": true,
    "decision": "pass",
    "requestedSlug": "socratic-dialog",
    "requestedVersion": "0.1.3",

    "securityPassed": true
```

A new headless Chromium context then navigated directly to the Skills route against that Gateway. The capture asserted the first-load UI and recorded outgoing WebSocket methods:

```text
Unavailable security badge present: false
```

On that same current-head browser run, the proof harness forced only the Skills route snapshot to `connected: false` while retaining the same real, request-capable `GatewayBrowserClient`. target.title: fix: keep newline-mode reply paragraphs as separate channel bubbles
target.body:
Closes #109032

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp users with automatic visible replies and `chunkMode: newline` would see multi-paragraph Codex runtime replies collapse into one bubble, while the same configuration with the OpenClaw runtime kept separate bubbles.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex finals arrive as one accumulated text blob. Shared outbound planning previously packed blank-line paragraphs up to the transport size limit before delivery, so coalescing could not separate them again. The fix stays in the configured delivery path (not the Codex projector):

- `planOutboundTextMessageUnits` with `chunkMode: newline` keeps each blank-line paragraph as its own unit; the transport limit only splits oversized paragraphs.
- `EmbeddedBlockChunker` force flushes with `flushOnParagraph` also preserve those boundaries, so a terminal flush of an under-max buffer does not re-merge paragraphs.

Length-mode delivery is unchanged. No Codex extension import of internal markdown packages.

## User Impact

With WhatsApp (or any channel) `streaming.chunkMode: newline`, multi-paragraph automatic replies from the Codex runtime deliver as separate bubbles, matching OpenClaw runtime behavior. Length-mode and single-paragraph replies are unaffected.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest on Windows 11 (Node v24.15.0), HEAD `5c1fa8fd86`:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/infra/outbound/message-plan.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-block-chunker.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/chunk.test.ts
# Test Files  3 passed (3)
# Tests  83 passed (83)
```

Coverage:

- newline planning keeps two short paragraphs as two outbound units under a 4000-char transport limit
- force + `flushOnParagraph` emits Codex-style multi-paragraph finals as separate chunks
- existing packing defaults for `chunkByParagraph` / `chunkTextWithMode` remain covered by `chunk.test.ts`

Real WhatsApp A/B (distinct outbound message IDs) still needs a live tenant or Mantis capture; unit evidence proves the planning and force-flush boundaries that the reporter A/B attributed to the Codex vs OpenClaw runtime gap.

target.title: feat(slack): support running as a real Slack user (user identity)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Today OpenClaw's Slack channel can only run as a Slack **app/bot** — it appears as an app in the member list, is `@mention`-gated, and fundamentally cannot participate in the places people actually talk: a bot can never join a 1:1 DM or an existing group DM. Operators who want an agent that behaves like a real teammate (posts under a human's name, gets DMed, replies in group DMs) have no supported way to do it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an opt-in, account-level `identity: "bot" | "user"` mode for the Slack plugin (default `"bot"`, so existing setups are unchanged).

`identity: "user"` authenticates as the authorizing human via a **user OAuth token (`xoxp`)** for all reads and writes, so messages appear under that person's name. A minimal **companion app** carries realtime events subscribed **"on behalf of users"** (Events API, Socket Mode or HTTP) — which is the *only* official mechanism to receive DMs and group DMs, since delivery is scoped to what the authorizing human can see and no bot can be present in those conversations.

We deliberately rejected the browser-session-token (`xoxc`/`xoxd`) "self-bot" approach used by chat bridges: it is unofficial, ToS-grey, session-fragile, and Slack is sunsetting the last legacy realtime path (classic apps end 2026-11-16). The user-token + companion-app path is the officially supported route.

Design notes: one identity-aware `resolveSlackOperationToken` (the duplicated `userTokenReadOnly` gate was removed); the human's own `user_id` (from `auth.test` on the user token) becomes the mention/DM target and the self-send dedupe source, so the agent never replies to its own messages; `@slack/bolt` runs token-less via `token: userToken` (verified against Bolt source). No `xoxc`/`xoxd`, no bot user required.

## User Impact

- Operators can opt a Slack account into acting as a **real person** (`identity: "user"`), including full DM and group-DM participation, with the companion app as invisible plumbing.
- **Existing bot setups are unaffected** — `identity` defaults to `"bot"` and all bot-identity behavior is byte-neutral; no config migration.
- Docs add the exact companion-app recipe (user scopes, on-behalf-of-user event subscriptions, Socket/HTTP config examples) in `docs/channels/slack.md`.

## Evidence

- **Full Slack plugin suite green**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack` → 121 files / 1922 tests passing, confirmed stable across 5 consecutive parallel runs (a shared-state test flake surfaced during review and was fixed — see the final commit).
- **Typecheck**: `tsgo:core` / `tsgo:extensions` / `tsgo:extensions:test` clean (Blacksmith Testbox).
- **Review**: each slice independently reviewed (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`); the transport's token-less Bolt startup and self-send dedupe were verified directly against `@slack/bolt` source; the token model against Slack's official docs.
- **Behavior-neutral for `identity: "bot"`**: no existing bot-identity assertions changed.

**Known validation gap (intentional, opt-in):** live delivery of bot-less user-scope `message.im`/`message.mpim` events is documented by Slack via the scope/visibility model but is thinly exercised in the wild; end-to-end verification in a live workspace is pending. Because the feature is opt-in and default-`bot`, this does not affect existing users — the live check is a fast-follow, and any Slack-side wrinkle is a documented follow-up rather than a regression.

target.title: fix(googlechat): surface reply send failures instead of silently dropping chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`deliverGoogleChatReply` (extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts:79-109 on `main`) wrapped every chunk send in a try/catch that only logged the error and kept looping. Two silent-loss paths resulted:

1. A failing `sendGoogleChatMessage` for any non-first chunk was logged and the chunk was dropped; the loop continued and the function resolved normally.
2. When the first-chunk typing-message update failed and the fallback resend also failed, that second failure was logged and swallowed too — the entire reply was lost.

The core reply dispatcher contract treats a rejected `deliver` as a failed delivery and a resolved one as visible delivery: `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts:476-483` awaits `options.deliver(...)` and only routes to `onError` / `failed-deliver` in `.catch`. Resolving after a swallowed send error therefore reported the turn as delivered while the user saw nothing (or only part of the reply).

## Why This Change Was Made

Restructure the chunk loop so the typing-update fallback stays, but any final send failure rejects out of `deliverGoogleChatReply`, matching the dispatcher contract. The typing-update catch is kept because a stale typing placeholder is recoverable — the same chunk is immediately resent as a new message, and only that resend failing is a real delivery failure. This mirrors the LINE sibling, which documents that a lost bubble "must surface as a partial delivery, not silent success" (extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts:217-219), and the same-channel precedent https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96646 ("throw on non-ok instead of parsing error body as success").

Fix classification: channel delivery error-propagation fix, additive behavior change only on the failure path; no config, SDK, or core changes.

## User Impact

- Google Chat reply send failures now surface through the dispatcher `onError` path instead of being counted as visible deliveries, so dropped or partially delivered replies are no longer reported as successfully sent.
- The existing typing-fallback behavior is unchanged when the resend succeeds.

## Evidence

### Integration-backed failure-path proof (real HTTP stack, loopback stub)

New committed regression test `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts` drives the production stack end to end against a local HTTP impersonator of the Google Chat API: `deliverGoogleChatReply` → `sendGoogleChatMessage` → `withGoogleChatResponse` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → real `google-auth-library` JWT signing and token exchange. Only global `fetch` is stubbed (rerouting `chat.googleapis.com` / `oauth2.googleapis.com` to `127.0.0.1`); the service-account key is a throwaway RSA key generated in-process, the stub issues the token, and the stub answers the second `spaces.messages` create with a real HTTP 500 error envelope. The deliver/onError wiring mirrors `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.ts:408-429`, and the outcome labels follow the dispatcher contract in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts:476-483`. No real credentials, endpoints, or user data anywhere.

Standalone transcript of the same flow (three-chunk reply, second create → 500), after the fix:

```
stub: POST /token (grant=jwt-bearer) -> 200 access_token=ya29.stub-token (redacted)
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #1 text="First chunk of the assistant reply." -> 200
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #2 text="Second chunk of the assistant reply." -> 500
runtime.error: [default] Google Chat text reply failed: Error: Google Chat API 500: {"error":{"code":500,"message":"stub: backend unavailable","status":"INTERNAL"}}
dispatcher: deliveryOutcome=failed-deliver
summary: tokenExchanges=1 messageCreates=2 createStatuses=[200,500] patchAttempts=0 onErrorCalls=1
```

Same stub, same input, pre-fix `monitor-reply-delivery.ts` from `origin/main` (reverse control): the 500 is logged and swallowed, the third chunk is still sent, and the dispatcher records the reply as delivered with `onError` never firing:

```
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #1 text="First chunk of the assistant reply." -> 200
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #2 text="Second chunk of the assistant reply." -> 500
runtime.error: Google Chat message send failed: Error: Google Chat API 500: {"error":{"code":500,...}}
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #3 text="Third chunk of the assistant reply." -> 200
dispatcher: deliveryOutcome=delivered
summary: tokenExchanges=1 messageCreates=3 createStatuses=[200,500,200] patchAttempts=0 onErrorCalls=0
```

Second after-fix scenario (typing placeholder already deleted upstream: `PATCH .../messages/typing` → 404, resend create → 500): the recoverable placeholder failure is logged, the resend failure rejects and reaches `onError`:

```
stub: PATCH /v1/spaces/AAA/messages/typing -> 404 (typing placeholder gone)
runtime.error: Google Chat message send failed: Error: Google Chat API 404: {"error":{"code":404,...}}
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #1 text="First chunk of the assistant reply." -> 500
runtime.error: [default] Google Chat text reply failed: Error: Google Chat API 500: {"error":{"code":500,...}}
dispatcher: deliveryOutcome=failed-deliver
summary: tokenExchanges=1 messageCreates=1 createStatuses=[500] patchAttempts=1 onErrorCalls=1
```

| | BEFORE (`origin/main` source) | AFTER (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Stub observed | 3 real `POST .../messages` (`[200,500,200]`) | 2 real `POST .../messages` (`[200,500]`), third chunk never attempted |
| `deliver` result | resolved — reply counted delivered, chunk 2 silently dropped | rejected with `Google Chat API 500: {...}` |
| Dispatcher outcome | `delivered`, `onError` never fires | `failed-deliver`, `onError` fires once with the API error |
| New integration test | 2 of 3 tests fail (reverse-verified) | 3/3 pass |

### Before vs after (same regression tests, same mocks)

| Scenario | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Non-first chunk send rejects | resolves; chunk dropped, loop continues | rejects with the send error |
| Typing update fails, fallback resend rejects | resolves; whole reply lost | rejects with the resend error |
| Typing update fails, fallback resend succeeds | resends, resolves (kept) | resends, resolves (unchanged) |

### Contract chain (source verified on `main`)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Channel deliver | `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.ts` | 408-421 | `deliver: async (payload) => { await deliverGoogleChatReply(...) }` |
| Channel onError | `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.ts` | 425-429 | `[accountId] Google Chat <kind> reply failed: <err>` |
| Swallowed failure (pre-fix) | `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts` | 95-107 | catch logs, drops chunk / swallows fallback failure, loop resolves |
| Dispatcher contract | `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts` | 476-483 | `await options.deliver(...)`; only `.catch` routes to `onError` / `failed-deliver` |
| Sibling precedent | `extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts` | 217-219 | lost bubble must surface as partial delivery, not silent success |

### Control-red (reverse verification)

Reverting only `monitor-reply-delivery.ts` to `origin/main` while keeping the new tests:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts
 Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
   × surfaces a failed non-first chunk send as a dispatcher-visible delivery failure
   × rejects when the resend after a typing-placeholder update failure also fails
     → Expected: "failed-deliver" / Received: "delivered" (500 logged and swallowed)
```

The mock-level suite shows the same inversion (`2 failed | 4 passed` on pre-fix source). With the fix restored, both suites are green.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

Full extension suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat` → 211 passed / 1 failed (212 total); the single failure (`setup.test.ts:236`, service-account setup-wizard flow) also fails on a clean `origin/main` checkout without this change (pre-existing, unrelated — same failure observed in the previous proof round before this PR touched anything).

### What was not tested

- A real Google Chat workspace send (requires live service-account credentials); the loopback impersonator covers the full production HTTP/auth/guard stack instead, including the real error-envelope parsing that builds the `Google Chat API 500: ...` message.
- Full-repo `tsgo` lanes left to CI.

### Impact-surface review

| File | Change | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts` | chunk loop restructured; send failures now propagate | covered by mock-level + integration regression tests |
| `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts` | +2 rejection tests; existing fallback test unchanged and green | 6/6 pass |
| `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts` | new integration suite: real HTTP stub, before/after dispatcher-visible outcomes | 3/3 pass; 2 fail on pre-fix source |

### Lint / typecheck / format

```
$ oxlint extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts   # exit 0
$ tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json (fresh buildinfo)                                                                                                    # 0 errors
$ oxfmt --check <all touched files>                                                                                                                                         # correct format
$ git diff --check origin/main                                                                                                                                              # clean
```

Base: 76e97ddcdb515f2af781a4b146d9e47eaacdf9e2 (`origin/main`). Head: a1cb28d8b3253761dd48e36bc51f426cd204787c.

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled on this PR.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- Land-ready: single commit, 3 files, googlechat-only; no core/SDK/config surface touched.
- Branch rebased onto current `origin/main` (76e97ddcdb) during this proof round.
- Scope discipline: only the swallowed-error path in `monitor-reply-delivery.ts` plus its colocated tests; the typing-fallback success path is byte-for-byte behavior-preserved.

</details>

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw cron run` (a manual/operator run) on a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot ("at") job used to delete the job on success — consuming the one-shot so its scheduled fire never happened (issue #83538). Manual runs also mutated `consecutiveErrors` / `consecutiveSkipped` counters and `nextRunAtMs`, corrupting the scheduled retry/backoff/next-run state that only real scheduler executions should own.

The root cause is that `applyJobResult()` had no notion of *who* triggered a run: manual, scheduled (timer), and the gateway on-exit watcher all shared one finalization path, so `shouldDelete` and the counter mutations fired for every successful run regardless of origin.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix threads an explicit `CronRunOrigin` (`"timer" | "watcher-terminal" | "operator"`) through cron finalization. `applyJobResult` derives `consumesOneShot` and `ownsSchedulerState` as `origin !== "operator"` and records `lastRunWasManual = origin === "operator"`, so operator runs record the outcome only (never consume a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot, never touch scheduler counters / `nextRunAtMs` / enabled state), while `timer` and `watcher-terminal` runs keep consuming and owning scheduler state — preserving the merged on-exit `deleteAfterRun` contract from #104550.

`origin` is kept strictly internal. It is **not** part of the public `CronServiceRunOptions`: exposing it there would let any in-process facade caller (plugin SDK, RPC handlers, tests) request `watcher-terminal` semantics and delete one-shots or mutate scheduler-owned counters/backoff/timing. Instead, the public `run` is always operator semantics, and the gateway on-exit watcher — the only legitimate non-operator caller, which already holds the concrete `CronService` instance — uses a concrete-only `CronService.runOnExitTerminal` entry (absent from `CronServiceContract` / `GatewayCronServiceContract`) to get consuming behavior. The invalid-persisted-run path (`skipInvalidPersistedManualRun`) also forwards the true caller origin instead of hard-coding `operator`, so an invalid watcher-terminal run keeps scheduler-owned semantics.

## User Impact

- Debugging/manually running a scheduled `deleteAfterRun` job no longer silently cancels its upcoming scheduled fire.
- Manual runs no longer corrupt retry backoff, auto-disable, or next-run timing of scheduled jobs.
- Gateway on-exit watcher-terminal one-shots continue to be consumed exactly as before (no regression for the #104550 contract).
- The scheduler-consuming origin is no longer reachable through the public cron API, so plugins/RPC/tests cannot accidentally (or intentionally) delete one-shots or mutate scheduler state via `run`.

## Evidence

Real-setup proof at the current head using a **real running OpenClaw gateway process and the real `openclaw cron` CLI** (not a vitest/function harness). Built from this head and run inside a `node:24-bookworm` container (container node v24.18.0; the repo engines floor is 24.15.0), against a real on-disk cron store (sqlite).

```
Head: c071ce7ca34e7a41e4fafab4a8863960fb9403c7
Gateway: OpenClaw 2026.7.2 (c071ce7)   dist/build-info.json commit = c071ce7c...

Built-artifact fix verification (fix compiled into the running gateway):
  dist/server-cron-*.js contains:
    async runOnExitTerminal(id, payload) { ... }
    run: (jobId, payload) => cron.runOnExitTerminal(jobId, payload)
  'watcher-terminal' occurs only inside runOnExitTerminal; the public run path
  forwards no origin.

PART A — OPERATOR PRESERVATION (real `openclaw cron run`)
  $ openclaw cron add "partA-ok-preserve" --at "+2h" --command "echo ..." --delete-after-run
    -> id 3c309f88..., nextRunAtMs 1784045230759
  $ openclaw cron run 3c309f88... --wait
    -> {"status":"ok", exitCode 0}          (operator path, success)
  $ openclaw cron get 3c309f88...
    -> job STILL PRESENT, enabled:true, deleteAfterRun:true,
       nextRunAtMs 1784045230759 (UNCHANGED), lastRunWasManual:true,
       no consecutiveErrors / no backoff mutation
  => successful operator run did NOT consume the one-shot, scheduler state intact.

PART B — WATCHER-TERMINAL CONSUMPTION (real gateway on-exit watcher cycle)
  $ openclaw cron add "partB-onexit-consume" --on-exit "sleep 8; echo ..." \
        --command "echo ..." --delete-after-run
  # real gateway watcher armed + spawned the watched process (seen in ps):
  #   bash -lc sleep 8   /   sleep 8
  [cron] cron-exit: watcher armed { jobId: a27c2044... }
  [cron] cron-exit: watched command exited; firing job { exitCode: 0 }
  $ openclaw cron get a27c2044...      -> "cron job not found"
  $ openclaw cron list                 -> only the 2 PART A jobs remain
  $ sqlite3 .../openclaw.sqlite 'select job_id from cron_jobs'  -> 2 rows (no partB)
  => real on-exit watcher-terminal run DID consume/delete the successful one-shot.

OVERALL: PASS — driven end-to-end through a live gateway + operator CLI + real
on-disk store. Operator and watcher-terminal origins are cleanly separated, and
the scheduler-consuming origin is unreachable from the public cron API.
```

Unit/regression coverage at head: the public `CronServiceContract.run` preserves a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot (operator semantics, no scheduler-state mutation) even though it can no longer request another origin, `CronService.runOnExitTerminal` still consumes a successful on-exit one-shot, and invalid watcher-terminal runs keep scheduler-owned semantics while operator invalid runs stay operator-attributed.

Persisted-state coverage for `lastRunWasManual` (`timer.backoff-config-readback.test.ts`, real on-disk sqlite store): a **fresh store** where a manual/operator error run persists `lastRunWasManual: true`, reloads from sqlite, and keeps the natural next-run slot (no backoff floor, `consecutiveErrors` untouched) so the scheduled fire still triggers on a fresh service state; and an **upgraded store** whose persisted job predates the field (no `lastRunWasManual` on disk) — on reload the absent field is treated as a scheduled run, so the error backoff window still applies and the past-due slot is correctly suppressed. This proves the new optional field degrades safely for both new and pre-existing stores.

### Proof equivalence: transcript head → current head

The live-setup transcript above was captured at `c071ce7c`. The branch head has since been rebased onto newer `main` (current head `c42041b0`). Scoped to the cron runtime surface exercised by the transcript (`src/cron/service/`, `src/gateway/server-cron.ts`), the full non-test delta between `c071ce7c` and the current head is:

- **`export`-keyword removals on now-module-local symbols** — `onTimer`, `executeJobCore` (`timer.ts`); `resetActiveCronTaskRunsForTests`, `CRON_TASK_RUN_SETTLEMENT_TRACKING_MAX_MS` (`active-run-cancellation.ts`); `DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS`, `AGENT_TURN_SAFETY_TIMEOUT_MS` (`timeout-policy.ts`). Values and in-module usage unchanged; no prod file outside each defining module imported them.
- **test-support extraction** — `timer.ts` and `active-run-cancellation.ts` now expose those test-only helpers via a `globalThis` symbol registered inside an `if (process.env.VITEST || process.env.NODE_ENV === "test")` guard, imported by new `*.test-support.ts` modules. This block is a no-op in a production gateway.
- **four appended `/* oxlint-disable max-lines */` directive comments** (`jobs.ts`, `ops.ts`, `timer.ts`, `server-cron.ts`).
- **rebased-in `main` change #104430 ("cap trigger script tool access")** — `mergeCronPayload` and its `toolsAllow` helpers moved out of `jobs.ts` into the new `src/cron/service/payload-merge.ts`, with cross-payload-kind `toolsAllow` marker handling. This is genuine upstream behavior on the `cron.update` payload-merge / trigger-script tool-access surface, disjoint from scheduler counters and one-shot consumption; it arrived through the rebase and is not part of this PR's proof scope.
- **`server-cron.ts` `toolsAllow` type-guard simplification** — the trigger-script call now reads `job.payload.toolsAllow` directly (valid once #104430 lifted `toolsAllow` to a shared `CronPayload` field) instead of gating on `kind === "agentTurn"`. This is on the trigger-script tool-access path, not the `runOnExitTerminal` / delete-after-run wiring.

None of these touch the delete-after-run / origin / backoff / one-shot-consumption / scheduler-state control flow. The `CronRunOrigin` threading, `consumesOneShot` / `ownsSchedulerState` (`origin !== "operator"`), `lastRunWasManual` (`origin === "operator"`), `shouldDelete = wouldDelete && consumesOneShot` in `timer.ts`, the `ops.ts` origin forwarding, and the `runOnExitTerminal` wiring in `server-cron.ts` are unchanged. The recorded operator-preservation and watcher-terminal-consumption behavior therefore holds on the current head. Reviewers can confirm the delta with:

```
git diff c071ce7c c42041b00bec162b9d7851010db37ad1bb56e818 -- src/cron/service/ src/gateway/server-cron.ts
```


### Follow-up fix: manual ok run must not strand the one-shot slot

A further defect on the same origin-threading surface: a **due** `deleteAfterRun` one-shot `at` job that receives an **operator (manual) ok run** keeps its `nextRunAtMs` preserved (operator runs do not consume the one-shot), but `computeJobNextRunAtMs`'s `at`-branch collapsed the pending slot to `undefined` whenever the last run status was `ok`. The next expired-slot maintenance recompute then wiped the slot, stranding the job as a zombie that never fires and never deletes. Existing coverage only exercised `skipped` runs, so the `ok` path was missed.

Fix: the ok-branch collapse in `computeJobNextRunAtMs` is now guarded by `lastRunWasManual !== true`, so only a scheduler-owned (timer) ok run retires the slot; manual/operator ok runs leave the pending scheduled fire intact. This reuses the already-persisted `lastRunWasManual` field, so it is restart-safe with no new state or migration (an absent field on a pre-upgrade store is treated as a scheduled run, preserving prior behavior). A regression test drives a manual ok run on a due deleteAfterRun one-shot through the maintenance recompute and a restart reload (slot preserved both times), then a real scheduled timer tick that fires and deletes it.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where external plugins could render and handle Discord callback buttons but could not submit a generic selected reply back into the originating agent conversation. This prevented channel-neutral quick-reply plugins from supporting Discord safely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `submitText` to the shared interactive-handler result contract and maps handled, authorized Discord submissions through the existing component inbound path. The submitted text retains the source component's session, agent, account, message, channel, thread, and reply context; declined, unauthorized, empty, malformed, failed, stale, and duplicate interactions do not submit it.

Telegram now uses the same canonical result type while retaining its existing transport behavior.

## User Impact

External plugins can implement generic Discord quick-reply buttons without creating detached agent turns or hard-coding product-specific callback behavior in core.

target.title: feat(ui): custodian onboarding surface with option cards and first-run handoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Phase 4 PR1 of the custodian onboarding redesign (plan: `docs/start/onboarding-redesign.md`). After the web Control UI's first-run model-setup wizard verifies inference, the user is currently dropped onto the plain dashboard. There is no conversational onboarding surface in the browser, and the phase-3 CLI browser handoff has no dedicated page to deep-link into.

## Why This Change Was Made

The redesign's north star is that onboarding is a conversation with OpenClaw (the system agent), not a form. This PR gives the web UI that surface: a custodian chat page in minimal onboarding chrome, structured choices rendered as option cards (max 4 options, exactly one recommended, always skippable), and a first-run handoff from the model-setup wizard into that conversation.

## User Impact

- New route `/custodian` (deep-linkable as `/custodian?onboarding=1` for the phase-3 CLI handoff; not in the sidebar nav). Renders a conversation with the system agent over the existing `openclaw.chat` gateway RPC (`welcomeVariant: "onboarding"`), with minimal chrome and one "Exit setup" control that restores normal chrome.
- New `openclaw-option-card` component: header chip, question, 2-4 option cards with optional descriptions, one recommended accent, always-present skip. Selection replies with the exact option label so the agent-harness user-input bridge parses it.
- Structured questions require an explicit hidden marker (`<!-- openclaw-user-input {json} -->`) in the reply; ordinary prose (including numbered lists) always stays plain text, and invalid markers degrade to text. Nothing emits the marker server-side yet — that is the phase 4 PR2 follow-up; until then the page is a plain conversation.
- First-run model-setup completion navigates to the custodian page instead of the dashboard; non-first-run wizard behavior is unchanged.
- Session ownership is bounded by gateway URL plus presented credentials: a client swap with different auth (same URL) clears the transcript and pending state and starts a fresh onboarding session, so conversations never leak across logins on a shared browser. Transport reconnects keep the conversation.

## Evidence

- UI unit tests: option-card (7), custodian page (14, incl. credential/bootstrap-token boundary, no-replay, and sensitive-verbatim regressions), structured-question parser (10), app-host/navigation/model-setup handoff — all green via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Browser E2E route tests: 3/3.
- `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint on touched files, `pnpm deadcode:exports`, i18n baseline/verify, `git diff --check`, `pnpm format` — all green.
- Live test on this Mac: vite dev UI connected to an isolated same-config gateway (port 18999) with a real system agent (openai/gpt-5.6-sol). Verified: `/custodian?onboarding=1` renders minimal chrome; onboarding welcome arrives via `openclaw.chat`; send round-trip ("help" → real system-agent reply); "Exit setup" restores full chrome on the chat page.
- Autoreview loop (Codex, branch mode, xhigh): four findings across three passes, all fixed with regression tests — session reset on token/password change (`a270ba22494`), bootstrap-token in the ownership key (`c0ad346a370`), no replay of ambiguous user turns + sensitive input sent verbatim (`eed62310ed6`). Final pass clean ("patch is correct", no actionable findings).

target.title: fix: prevent silent message loss from EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError
target.body:
## Summary

When the OpenAI SDK retried an `ECONNRESET` internally (default `maxRetries=2`), the session write lock was released during the retry window. Incoming steering messages could then modify the transcript without updating the fence, causing a fingerprint mismatch on `reacquireAfterPrompt()`. The resulting `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` was caught by `model-fallback.ts` which aborted the run, and the outer reply pipeline produced no user-visible output — the message was silently lost.

## What Problem This Solves

A user's steering message could be silently dropped during a session takeover. The takeover was made more likely by an in-window SDK retry running against a released session lock, and when it fired the reply pipeline fell into a generic failure branch that emitted no actionable output. This fix closes the race that widened the takeover window and converts the takeover into an explicit, actionable reply so the user knows to resend.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two invariants must hold together. First, no in-window SDK retry may run inside the embedded prompt-lock release window, because that window releases the session lock across the model call and an in-window retry re-admits the session-takeover race (#87180). Second, an unconfigured user's bare connection and request-timeout resilience must not regress — so that resilience moves to the orchestrator layer, where each retry re-acquires the session lock and cannot widen any single release window. When a takeover does occur, the runner must surface resend guidance rather than a silent or generic failure.

## Root Cause Chain

```
API ECONNRESET
  → OpenAI SDK default maxRetries=2, internal retry
  → session write lock released during retry window
  → incoming message arrives via queueHandle.queueMessage
  → activeSession.steer writes directly (bypassing withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites)
  → transcript changes without updating fence
  → original attempt reacquireAfterPrompt() fingerprint mismatch
  → EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError thrown
  → model-fallback.ts aborts the run
  → outer layer hits generic failure branch
  → assistantTexts/payloads never enter buildReplyPayloads()
  → message silently lost (user sees generic error or nothing)
```

## Fix

Seven coordinated changes that address the bug at multiple layers:

### 1. Wrap steering in `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites` (`attempt.ts`)
Steering writes that arrive during prompt lock release now go through `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites`, keeping fence tracking consistent and preventing the fingerprint mismatch that triggers the takeover error.

### 2. Dedicated error handler for takeover (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `failover-error.ts`)
Added `isEmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError()` export and a dedicated catch block in `runAgentTurnWithFallback`. Instead of falling into the generic failure branch (silent loss), users now receive a clear message asking them to resend. When a takeover wraps a preserved prompt error (billing, rate-limit, context-overflow), the original error is unwrapped and classified normally — only pure takeover errors return resend guidance.

### 3. Pin SDK retries to 0 inside the embedded prompt lock window (`attempt.ts`, `attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Extracted `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` helper that wraps the session's `streamFn` with `{ maxRetries: 0, ...options }`. The in-window default is **unconditionally 0** — the configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries` is deliberately NOT injected here, because the prompt-lock window releases the session lock across the model call and an in-window SDK retry would run against a released lock and re-admit the session-takeover race (#87180). An explicit per-call `maxRetries` still overrides (spread last). Unconfigured connection/timeout resilience is instead restored at the orchestrator layer (see #6, #7), where each retry re-acquires the session lock and cannot widen any single release window. Non-embedded callers retain the SDK default retry behavior (maxRetries=2).

### 4. Forward maxRetries through native OpenAI transport (`openai-transport-stream.ts`)
`buildOpenAISdkRequestOptions` previously accepted only `model` and `signal`, dropping the `maxRetries` injected by `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault`. Added `maxRetries` parameter and forwarded it through all three native transport call sites (Responses, Azure Responses, Completions). When `maxRetries` is the only option present, the function now returns an object instead of `undefined` so the SDK receives the override.

### 5. Phase tracking in `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (`attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Added a `phase` field (`prompt_reacquire`, `cleanup`, `write`, `fence_check`) for better diagnostics when this error does occur. Backward compatible — the phase parameter is optional with existing call sites unchanged.

### 6. Restore unconfigured connection-error retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`)
Disabling SDK retries inside the prompt-lock release window (#3) is required so an in-window retry cannot widen the takeover race — but for users who have **not** configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, it also dropped the SDK's default retry of bare connection errors (`ECONNRESET`, `socket hang up`, `Connection error.`) that carry no leading HTTP status. This is restored at the orchestrator layer, where the existing one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` re-runs the full primary→fallback cycle and **re-acquires the session lock per attempt**, so it does not widen any single release window. The transient-retry gate now fires on `(isTransientHttp || isConnectionError)`; the new `isConnectionError` predicate reuses the canonical `INTERRUPTED_NETWORK_ERROR_RE` so it stays in sync with failover routing. In-window `maxRetries:0` is unchanged. This keeps the takeover-race fix intact while preserving unconfigured-user connection resilience.

### 7. Restore unconfigured request-timeout retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`)
The orchestrator transient-retry restore in #6 left a symmetric gap: in addition to bare connection errors, the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs retry request-**timeout** transport errors by default, and after the in-window `maxRetries:0`, an unconfigured single-model user's timeout error is rethrown to the same outer gate — which only matched HTTP-status transients and connection errors, dropping timeout retry entirely (multi-model users were unaffected because failover already routes timeouts). The transient-retry gate now also fires on a new `isTransientTimeout` predicate (`isTimeoutErrorMessage`, the existing canonical timeout classifier), with its own `Transient timeout error` diagnostic label so the cause stays distinguishable in logs. The timeout disjunct is deliberately scoped to exclude non-transport timeout-looking messages: (a) timeout-only fallback summaries (`!isFallbackSummaryError` — multi-model failover already ran, so a redundant retry is wrong; this guard is scoped to the timeout disjunct only and does not change the connection path), and (b) CLI subprocess budget kills and Codex app-server bridge failures (`!hasDedicatedNonTransportTimeoutCopy` — these are subprocess kills / bridge failures, not transport timeouts, and have their own surfaced copy and replay handling). The one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` budget is shared, so timeout retry is bounded exactly like the connection retry. The connection-retry path semantics from #6 are unchanged. The timeout disjunct additionally excludes local non-provider runtime coordination errors (e.g. `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`, whose message reads as `session file locked (timeout ...ms)`) via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier: retrying any model would hit the same local condition, so these abort the fallback chain rather than re-run as a transport timeout.

## User Impact

- A transient connection reset mid-turn no longer risks losing the reply: the orchestrator retries the whole cycle once (with the session lock re-acquired) and delivers the assistant reply.
- When a session is genuinely taken over (new input arrived while the previous turn was still running), the user receives an explicit prompt to resend rather than silence or a non-actionable generic error.
- No new configuration is introduced; existing single-model users regain connection/timeout resilience, and multi-model users are unaffected.

## Evidence

Two complementary proofs cover this fix, both green at the current head `413a69e6d83f6c1612e2bb7aea9192a49a4a3b25`:

1. **Orchestrator-level proof** — an exact-head e2e test (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-takeover-live.e2e.test.ts`) that drives the real `runAgentTurnWithFallback` and asserts the user-facing reply.
2. **Real-process live proof** — a standalone real Node process (not vitest) that imports the real `src/**` modules and drives the real `openai-completions` transport over real HTTP against a loopback fake model server, capturing real terminal output.

Both drive the fix end to end through real components rather than hand-built errors; the second is a strict upgrade over scaffolded reply/fallback boundaries because the transport fault and the takeover are surfaced by the production code paths themselves.

### Proof 1 — orchestrator-level e2e (`agent-runner-takeover-live.e2e.test.ts`)

**What is real (no hand-built errors, no mocked runner internals):**
- A real temp session transcript file on disk.
- A real local `node:http` server acting as the model `baseUrl` (`api: openai-completions`).
- The real `openai-completions` transport stream fn (`createOpenAICompletionsTransportStreamFn`) doing real HTTP I/O.
- The real embedded prompt-lock controller + fence (`createEmbeddedAttemptSessionLockController`), wired through the real `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` (pins SDK `maxRetries` to 0) and `installPromptSubmissionLockRelease` — exactly as `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` wires them in production.
- The real connection/transient classification (`isConnectionError` / `isTransientHttpError` / `isTimeoutErrorMessage` from `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`) and the real failover classification (`isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError`), consumed by the real `runAgentTurnWithFallback` retry gate and takeover catch.

The only injected variables are at real boundaries: a dropped TCP socket (Scenario A) and a concurrent unowned transcript rewrite (Scenario B). The reply-pipeline boundary is scaffolded with the same mock surface as the existing `agent-runner-execution.test.ts`, plus a thin `runWithModelFallback` stand-in that runs the real candidate closure once and propagates exactly as the real `runWithModelFallback` does (re-throw on failure, return on success).

**Scenario A — pure transient transport fault.** The model server resets the socket on request #1, then succeeds on the retry. Because SDK retries are pinned to 0 inside the released-lock window, the SDK does not re-issue in-window; the orchestrator retries the whole cycle exactly once via `consumeTransientHttpRetry()`. Observed and asserted:
- Bounded provider request count `== 2` — one failed request plus exactly one orchestrator retry (the SDK did not retry in-window).
- The turn succeeded with a **visible** assistant reply containing `OK` (not silent loss).
- The transient-connection diagnostic `Transient connection error before reply (...). Retrying once in 2500ms.` was emitted exactly once.
- The reply operation was not failed on the recovery path.

**Scenario B — organic session takeover → resend guidance.** While the real model call holds the released prompt lock, a concurrent unowned rewrite of the same session transcript changes the session-file fingerprint, so `reacquireAfterPrompt` throws `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` **organically** inside the wrapped call's `finally`. Observed and asserted:
- Provider request count `== 1` — no silent in-window SDK retry.
- The user-facing reply is the exact resend-guidance literal produced by the real catch path at `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts:3123`: `⚠️ Your message was interrupted because new input arrived while the previous turn was still in progress. Please resend your message.`
- A `run_failed` lifecycle terminal was recorded via the reply operation.
- The takeover is a non-provider coordination error, so the fallback chain aborts rather than burning model candidates.

**Revert-resistance (each assertion is load-bearing):**
- Disabling the `maxRetries` pin makes Scenario A fail: the SDK silently retries in-window, the orchestrator never engages, and the transient diagnostic count is 0.
- Removing the takeover rewrite makes Scenario B fall back to generic error text instead of the resend guidance.

**Reproduce:**

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-takeover-live.e2e.test.ts
```

**Run summary (exact head `413a69e6d83f6c1612e2bb7aea9192a49a4a3b25`):**

```
 RUN  v4.1.9 <workdir>/openclaw-pr-workdirs/pr-89039

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Duration  31.15s
```

### Proof 2 — real-process live proof (standalone Node process, real HTTP)

This proof does not use vitest. A standalone throwaway harness runs under a real `node v24.15.0` process, imports the real `src/**` modules by absolute path, and drives the real `openai-completions` transport over real HTTP against a loopback-only fake model server on an ephemeral port. It runs fully isolated (`OPENCLAW_HOME`/`HOME`/`TMPDIR`), never touching the running system gateway, and captures the real terminal output — including the production `[provider-transport-fetch]` logger lines. Both scenarios passed (process exit 0, `ALL CHECKS PASSED`).

**Scenario A — real socket destroy → delivered reply.** The model server performs a real TCP socket destroy on request #1. The real transport surfaces `UND_ERR_SOCKET` / `fetch failed` through the production `[provider-transport-fetch]` logger; the real classifier reports `isConnectionError=true` / `isTransientHttpError=false`; the whole cycle is retried once; request #2 streams `OK`. Proven: **request count == 2** (SDK retries pinned to 0 in-window, so the single retry is the orchestrator's, not the SDK's), a **visible "OK" reply**, and **no silent loss**.

**Scenario B — organic session takeover → resend guidance.** While the real model call holds the released prompt lock, a concurrent unowned rewrite of the same session file changes its fingerprint, and `reacquireAfterPrompt` throws `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (phase `prompt_reacquire`) **organically**. Proven: **request count == 1** (no silent in-window SDK retry), the error is a real non-provider coordination error, and the orchestrator maps it to the exact resend-guidance literal.

**Captured real terminal output (redacted — username, absolute paths, and ephemeral ports scrubbed):**

```
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=mlx api=openai-completions model=probe-model method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/v1/chat/completions timeoutMs=900000 proxy=none policy=custom
model server: request #1 received -> destroying socket (real transport fault)
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] error provider=mlx api=openai-completions model=probe-model elapsedMs=253 name=TypeError code=undefined causeName=SocketError causeCode=UND_ERR_SOCKET message=fetch failed
cycle threw: "Connection error."
real classifier: isConnectionError=true isTransientHttpError=false
Transient connection error before reply (Connection error.). Retrying once in 2500ms. (orchestrator-equivalent gate)
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=mlx api=openai-completions model=probe-model method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/v1/chat/completions timeoutMs=900000 proxy=none policy=custom
model server: request #2 received -> streaming completion "OK"
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=mlx api=openai-completions model=probe-model status=200 elapsedMs=65 contentType=text/event-stream
PASS — real transport surfaced a bare connection error (isConnectionError)
PASS — connection drop is NOT a leading-HTTP-status transient
PASS — bounded request count == 2 (one reset + one orchestrator retry)
PASS — delivered assistant reply contains "OK" (no silent loss)
=== Scenario A complete ===

=== Scenario B: organic session takeover -> resend guidance ===
model server: request #1 received -> holding open until rewrite
concurrent unowned writer: rewriting session file out of band (steering append)
prompt window threw: EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: <ISOLATED_TMP>/session.jsonl (phase: prompt_reacquire)
PASS — prompt window threw an error (not a silent drop)
PASS — error is a real EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError
PASS — takeover is a non-provider coordination error (fallback chain aborts)
PASS — single request: no silent in-window SDK retry
orchestrator maps this coordination error -> resend guidance literal:
  ⚠️ Your message was interrupted because new input arrived while the previous turn was still in progress. Please resend your message.
=== Scenario B complete ===

ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

### Scope of this proof

This is strong real-transport + real-coordination component proof captured from live processes — a strict upgrade over scaffolded reply/fallback boundaries. The connection reset is a real TCP socket destroy surfaced by the real `openai-completions` transport over real HTTP, the classification and the bounded single retry use the real predicates, the recovery comes back over a real second HTTP call (`status=200`), and the takeover is triggered organically by a real concurrent file rewrite during a real held-lock window.

It does **not** boot the full installed gateway with a real channel transport (WhatsApp/Telegram/Discord) delivering to a real client. That is because a real channel needs external provider credentials plus live third-party services, while the model side must be a local deterministic fake to reproduce the reset-then-succeed sequence — a real paid model endpoint could not be made to reset then succeed on demand. This is a provisioning/credentials constraint, not a Node-version or code blocker: the model/provider and runtime-coordination path is faithfully reproduced end to end. A literal installed channel roundtrip would need a box provisioned with real (or sandbox) channel + model credentials.

### What was not tested

The configured provider retry-budget question — whether `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries` is preserved through the outer whole-attempt retries — is intentionally **out of scope** for this PR and tracked as a follow-up. target.title: refactor(memory-wiki): move compiled cache to plugin state
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory plugins could only contribute synchronous system-prompt text. Memory Wiki therefore persisted its compiled agent digest and claim index in legacy state files, then read those files during prompt assembly. That created a prompt-path filesystem dependency, stale-owner risk, and cache lifecycle behavior outside the plugin state owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one narrow async memory prompt-preparation registration. The agent run validates stable owner and vault-instance identity, loads prepared state before prompt assembly, and hands an immutable snapshot to synchronous prompt builders. Recompilation atomically replaces the snapshot; owner removal deletes its state.

Memory Wiki now stores its rebuildable compiled snapshot as a plugin blob in shared SQLite. Compile publishes one atomic replacement, prompt preparation and queries load the same snapshot, inactive owners are removed at plugin start, and stale legacy files are cleanup-only doctor debt. There is no file migration, polling, watcher, process decoded cache, or prompt-path filesystem I/O.

Context-engine assembly executes inside the same prepared-memory scope, including sandbox context, so custom engines preserve the async supplements without changing the synchronous context-engine contract.

AI-assisted implementation. Maintainer-requested architecture and migration.

## User Impact

Memory Wiki prompts and queries use one lifecycle-owned compiled snapshot. Restarts reload the SQLite blob, recompiles replace it atomically, removed vault owners lose their cached state, and old cache files are safely deleted by doctor instead of being read or migrated.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/compiled-cache.integration.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/prompt-section.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/index.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/vault.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/doctor-contract-api.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/bridge.test.ts test/scripts/check-database-first-legacy-stores.test.ts` — 550 tests passed.

target.title: fix(provider-error): keep error body truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

`formatProviderError` in `packages/ai/src/utils/provider-error.ts` truncates error response bodies at 4000 characters using `String.prototype.slice()`, which can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair and produce a dangling invalid character at the truncation boundary. Replaced with `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` which preserves surrogate pair integrity.

What changed: One line in `readBody` — `.slice(0, MAX_ERROR_BODY_LENGTH)` replaced by `truncateUtf16Safe(body, MAX_ERROR_BODY_LENGTH)` plus added the import.

What NOT changed: No behavioral change for sub-4000-char bodies. No change to error propagation, HTTP status handling, or any other runtime behavior. The function contract (returns truncated body string with "[truncated]" suffix) is unchanged.

Fixes #109974

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When a provider error response body is at or over 4000 characters and contains surrogate pair characters (emoji, CJK Extension B), the truncation cuts through the pair, producing an invalid character in the logged error message.

**Root Cause**: `readBody` in `packages/ai/src/utils/provider-error.ts:52` uses `.slice(0, MAX_ERROR_BODY_LENGTH)`. JavaScript's `.slice()` operates on UTF-16 code units and can split a surrogate pair at position 4000.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, MAX_ERROR_BODY_LENGTH)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(body, MAX_ERROR_BODY_LENGTH)` which detects whether position 4000 falls inside a surrogate pair by checking the code unit at that boundary. If it lands on a high surrogate (first half of a pair), the boundary is moved one code unit earlier to keep the pair completely intact rather than leaving a lone half behind.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic / Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node scripts/evidence-utf16-truncation.mjs` — standalone script that replicates `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` and compares it with `body.slice()` against a 4004-char body (3999 ASCII + 🤖 emoji + "END"). Script committed in this PR.

**After-fix evidence**:
```
========================================================================
  PR #109974: UTF-16 safe truncation in formatProviderError
  HEAD: e21db75baf8
========================================================================

  body length    = 4004  (prefix 3999 + emoji 2 + 'END' 3)
  MAX            = 4000
  emoji codepoints at 3999-4000: \uD83E \uDD16
  slice(0,4000) captures index 0..3999: includes high surrogate at 3999, misses low at 4000

  Raw slice truncated length:  4000
  Raw safe truncated length:   3999
  Raw slice dangling surrogate: YES at index 3999 (\uD83E)
  Raw safe dangling surrogate:  no

── OLD (body.slice) ──
  total length:      4015
  dangling surrogate: YES (\uD83E at position 3999)
  tail (last 30):    "XXXXXXXXXXXXXX\ud83e... [truncated]"

── NEW (truncateUtf16Safe) ──
  total length:      4014
  dangling surrogate: no
  tail (last 30):    "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX... [truncated]"

  Result: OLD outputs a broken \uD83E dangling surrogate; NEW is clean.
```

**Observed result after the fix**: `.slice(0, 4000)` ends on the high surrogate (U+D83E) of the 🤖 emoji, producing a dangling surrogate. `truncateUtf16Safe` detects this and moves the boundary back by 1 code unit, returning a complete, valid string.

**What was not tested**: Full Gateway runtime with real provider error responses. The change is a pure function swap identical to the existing pattern used in 100+ files across the codebase.

## Tests and validation

The accompanying `scripts/evidence-utf16-truncation.mjs` is a reproducible evidence script.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low — pure function change; ASCII behavior identical, non-BMP strictly safer

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703
